entries.breaker_note: Check the Zero base, repeated-addition recurrence, and natural-number product correspondence.
entries.implementer_note: Induct on x, unfold Mul in the successor case, and use AddCorrect to normalize the recursive result.

entries.title: Division and Modulus
error_states: A zero divisor is accepted — `DivMod(x,Zero)` is defined despite the required precondition.
The else-branch recursive call does not decrease, causing nontermination.
Pair destructuring swaps quotient and remainder, or increments the wrong component.
The quotient and remainder fail reconstruction — `Add(Mul(d,y),m) != x`.
The remainder is not smaller than the divisor — `Less(m,y) == false`.

laws.name: Nonzero divisor domain
laws.equation: defined(DivMod(x,y)) => y != Zero
laws.falsifier: exhibit x with DivMod(x,Zero) accepted

laws.name: Subtraction decreases the rank
laws.equation: !Less(x,y) && y != Zero => UnaryToNat(Sub(x,y)) < UnaryToNat(x)
laws.falsifier: exhibit x,y satisfying the premise with Sub(x,y) not smaller

laws.name: DivMod base case
laws.equation: Less(x,y) && y != Zero => DivMod(x,y) == (Zero,x)
laws.falsifier: exhibit x,y satisfying the premise with a different pair

laws.name: DivMod recursive step
laws.equation: !Less(x,y) && y != Zero && DivMod(Sub(x,y),y) == (d',m') => DivMod(x,y) == (Suc(d'),m')
laws.falsifier: exhibit x,y,d',m' satisfying the premise but not the quotient/remainder step

laws.name: Pair pattern binding
laws.equation: For r == (d0,m0), let (d,m) := r implies d == d0 && m == m0
laws.falsifier: exhibit a pair whose pattern binding changes or swaps a component

laws.name: Division-modulus correctness
laws.equation: For (d,m) == DivMod(x,y), y != Zero => Add(Mul(d,y),m) == x && Less(m,y)
laws.falsifier: exhibit x,y with y != Zero violating reconstruction or the remainder bound

entries.breaker_note: Red tests must cover the nonzero-divisor contract, decreasing subtraction, pair component order, reconstruction, and the strict remainder bound.
entries.implementer_note: Use SubCorrect before the recursive call with the natural decreases metric in 7.4.0, or structural inclusion from 7.4.1; use pair patterns from 7.4.2 and prove the two correctness clauses by cases as in 7.4.3.

entries.title: Specification
error_states: the sorting function returns exactly the input elements but in non-ascending order
the sorting function returns an ordered list that drops a duplicate or introduces an element
the Ordered predicate checks only the first adjacent pair and accepts a later inversion
a keyed sort reorders distinct records with equal keys, so sortedness and multiset preservation hold but stability fails

laws.name: Ordered output
laws.equation: For every input list xs: Ordered(S(xs)), where S is the candidate sorting function and Ordered is the ascending adjacent-pair predicate.
laws.falsifier: exhibit xs with !Ordered(S(xs))

laws.name: Global meaning of Ordered
laws.equation: For every integer list xs and natural indices i,j: Ordered(xs) && i <= j && j < Length(xs) => At(xs,i) <= At(xs,j), where At(xs,k) is zero-based lookup.
laws.falsifier: exhibit xs,i,j with Ordered(xs), i <= j < Length(xs), and At(xs,i) > At(xs,j)

laws.name: Same-element multiplicities
laws.equation: For every input xs and integer p: Count(S(xs),p) = Count(xs,p), where Count(xs,p) is the number of occurrences of p.
laws.falsifier: exhibit xs,p with Count(S(xs),p) != Count(xs,p)

laws.name: Stable projection
laws.equation: For every input xs and key p: ProjectKey(S(xs),p) = ProjectKey(xs,p), where ProjectKey retains, in order, exactly the records whose key is p; for integer lists this is Project(xs,p).
laws.falsifier: exhibit xs,p with ProjectKey(S(xs),p) != ProjectKey(xs,p)

entries.breaker_note: Section 8.0 makes sorting a conjunction: test order, multiplicity, and, when records have keys, equal-key order. Subsection 8.0.0 also warrants testing that the recursive Ordered definition implies order between arbitrary positions.
entries.implementer_note: Define specification-only predicates first, then prove their expected meaning. Use the recursive AllOrdered proof from 8.0.0: reduce both indices through the tail, and combine adjacent order with the induction hypothesis when the first index is zero.

entries.title: Insertion Sort
error_states: Insert places y after an element larger than y, so an ordered input produces an unordered output
Insert drops y, duplicates y, or loses an existing element while still producing an ordered list
InsertionSort sorts the tail but fails to insert the original head, so the result is not a rearrangement of the input
the helper lemma claims Insert always returns an ordered list without requiring its input list to be ordered

laws.name: Insert preserves order
laws.equation: For every integer y and list xs: Ordered(xs) => Ordered(Insert(y,xs)).
laws.falsifier: exhibit y,xs with Ordered(xs) and !Ordered(Insert(y,xs))

laws.name: Insert preserves projected elements
laws.equation: For every y,xs,p: Project(Cons(y,xs),p) = Project(Insert(y,xs),p), where Project retains all occurrences equal to p in list order.
laws.falsifier: exhibit y,xs,p with Project(Cons(y,xs),p) != Project(Insert(y,xs),p)

laws.name: Insertion Sort is ordered
laws.equation: For every list xs: Ordered(InsertionSort(xs)).
laws.falsifier: exhibit xs with !Ordered(InsertionSort(xs))

laws.name: Insertion Sort preserves projected elements
laws.equation: For every list xs and integer p: Project(xs,p) = Project(InsertionSort(xs),p).
laws.falsifier: exhibit xs,p with Project(xs,p) != Project(InsertionSort(xs),p)

entries.breaker_note: Test Insert independently because its two preservation laws are the tightest witnesses for the whole sort. Include an unordered xs against any over-strong InsertOrdered contract; the section explicitly discovers that Ordered(xs) is necessary.
entries.implementer_note: Mirror each recursive function with a lemma and follow the function's match and branch structure. Strengthen the helper lemma, not executable Insert, with Ordered(xs), then let the outer proof call the helper exactly where the algorithm calls Insert.

entries.title: Merge Sort
error_states: Split returns halves with the requested lengths but drops, duplicates, or reorders an element, so Append(left,right) != xs
one recursive MergeSortAux branch receives a length that is not strictly smaller than len, so recursion need not terminate
Merge chooses the larger head first or otherwise creates an inversion even though both inputs are ordered
Merge drops or duplicates occurrences, so its result is ordered but its projection differs from the appended input projections
MergeSortAux returns an ordered list assembled from the halves but the final list does not contain exactly the original elements

laws.name: Split is an exact partition
laws.equation: For n <= Length(xs), let (left,right) = Split(xs,n): Length(left) = n && Length(right) = Length(xs) - n && Append(left,right) = xs.
laws.falsifier: exhibit xs,n,left,right with n <= Length(xs), (left,right) = Split(xs,n), and either Length(left) != n, Length(right) != Length(xs)-n, or Append(left,right) != xs

laws.name: Both recursive lengths descend
laws.equation: For natural len with len >= 2: len/2 < len && len - len/2 < len, where / is natural-number division.
laws.falsifier: exhibit natural len >= 2 with len/2 >= len or len-len/2 >= len

laws.name: Merge preserves order
laws.equation: For all lists xs,ys: Ordered(xs) && Ordered(ys) => Ordered(Merge(xs,ys)).
laws.falsifier: exhibit xs,ys with Ordered(xs), Ordered(ys), and !Ordered(Merge(xs,ys))

laws.name: Merge preserves projected elements
laws.equation: For all ordered xs,ys and integer p: Project(Merge(xs,ys),p) = Append(Project(xs,p),Project(ys,p)).
laws.falsifier: exhibit ordered xs,ys and p with Project(Merge(xs,ys),p) != Append(Project(xs,p),Project(ys,p))

laws.name: Merge Sort contract
laws.equation: For every xs,p: Ordered(MergeSort(xs)) && Project(MergeSort(xs),p) = Project(xs,p).
laws.falsifier: exhibit xs,p with !Ordered(MergeSort(xs)) or Project(MergeSort(xs),p) != Project(xs,p)

entries.breaker_note: Attack Split, Merge, and the two recursive sizes separately before testing the end-to-end sort; those laws pinpoint partition, merge, and termination faults. The same-elements test must preserve multiplicity, not merely set membership.
entries.implementer_note: Use len as the explicit decreases metric because the split prefix is not structurally known to be part of xs. For 8.2.2, calculate from the complex side, establish ordered inputs before invoking MergeSameElements, apply both induction hypotheses, distribute Project across Append, and finish with Append(left,right) = xs.

entries.title: Summary
error_states: a test suite accepts a sorter solely because its output is ordered, overlooking that elements were lost or invented
a test suite accepts a sorter solely because it preserves the multiset, overlooking that the output remains unsorted
a sorter of keyed records preserves keys and order by key but reverses records within an equal-key group

laws.name: Complete sorting specification
laws.equation: For every xs: Ordered(S(xs)) && Multiset(S(xs)) = Multiset(xs), where S is a sorting routine and Multiset records each element's multiplicity.
laws.falsifier: exhibit xs with !Ordered(S(xs)) or Multiset(S(xs)) != Multiset(xs)

laws.name: Stable equal-key order
laws.equation: For every xs and key p: ProjectKey(S(xs),p) = ProjectKey(xs,p), where ProjectKey preserves the original sequence of records whose key is p.
laws.falsifier: exhibit xs,p with ProjectKey(S(xs),p) != ProjectKey(xs,p)

entries.breaker_note: Treat sortedness and same-elements as independent axes, and add the projection law when stability is promised. A green result on only one axis is not sorting correctness.
entries.implementer_note: Choose a specification form that exposes useful algebra: multiset or projection preservation avoids proving a complicated permutation relation and composes through recursive algorithms.

entries.title: Grouping Declarations into Modules
error_states: a qualified call intended for ListLibrary.Append resolves to another module's same-named Append, replacing list concatenation with an unrelated operation
ListLibrary.Append violates associativity, so regrouping three concatenations changes the resulting list

laws.name: Qualified-name isolation
laws.equation: Resolve(M,n) = declaration M.n, where Resolve is qualified lookup; if modules M1 and M2 both declare n, Resolve(M1,n) and Resolve(M2,n) remain distinct declarations.
laws.falsifier: exhibit modules M1,M2 and name n with M1 != M2, both declaring n, but Resolve(M1,n) = Resolve(M2,n)

laws.name: List append associativity
laws.equation: For all lists xs,ys,zs: Append(Append(xs,ys),zs) = Append(xs,Append(ys,zs)).
laws.falsifier: exhibit xs,ys,zs with Append(Append(xs,ys),zs) != Append(xs,Append(ys,zs))

entries.breaker_note: When modules contain same-named operations, write laws against the qualified declaration so a test cannot silently exercise the wrong function. Preserve the algebraic lemmas grouped with the datatype, such as AppendAssociative.
entries.implementer_note: Keep the datatype, its operations, and their lemmas in one module, and qualify external references through that module's name. This makes name resolution and proof dependencies explicit.

entries.title: Module Imports
error_states: ModuleB refers to sibling ModuleA without importing it, leaving ModuleA unresolved in ModuleB
import A = ModuleA binds A to the wrong module, so A.Plus computes a different operation than ModuleA.Plus
the import graph contains ModuleA -> ModuleB -> ModuleA, violating the required module hierarchy

laws.name: No implicit sibling visibility
laws.equation: Sibling(A,B) && !Imports(B,A) => A notin Scope(B), where Scope(B) is the set of module names resolvable inside B.
laws.falsifier: exhibit sibling modules A,B with !Imports(B,A) but A in Scope(B)

laws.name: Import alias binding
laws.equation: After import a = A inside B: ResolveB(a) = A, where ResolveB is module-name lookup in B.
laws.falsifier: exhibit modules A,B and alias a with import a = A in B but ResolveB(a) != A

laws.name: Acyclic imports
laws.equation: For every module M: !ReachImportsPlus(M,M), where ReachImportsPlus is reachability by one or more import edges.
laws.falsifier: exhibit modules M0,...,Mk with k >= 1 and imports M0 -> M1 -> ... -> Mk -> M0

entries.breaker_note: Model imports as a directed graph and test both scope and acyclicity. Alias tests should identify the exact target module, not just establish that the alias resolves.
entries.implementer_note: Add every cross-module dependency through an explicit import and use a local alias when repeated qualification would obscure the proof. Keep the import relation hierarchical so modules cannot depend cyclically on one another.

entries.title: Export Sets
error_states: a declaration listed with provides leaks its body or datatype constructors, letting a client depend on a private representation
an exported function signature mentions Parity while Parity is absent from the exported view, leaving the client interface malformed
a revealed function body refers to hidden constructors Even or Odd, so the exported view contains unresolved names
a wildcard export exposes a newly added helper, unexpectedly enlarging the public interface and allowing clients to couple to it

laws.name: Provides exports only the contract
laws.equation: Provides(M,d) => Exported(M,d) = Signature(d) && Body(d) notin ClientView(M), where Signature includes the name, types, parameters, and specification clauses.
laws.falsifier: exhibit module M and declaration d with Provides(M,d) but Body(d) or a hidden datatype constructor is in ClientView(M)

laws.name: Reveals exports contract and definition
laws.equation: Reveals(M,d) => Exported(M,d) = Signature(d) + Body(d), where + denotes inclusion of both parts in the client view.
laws.falsifier: exhibit module M and declaration d with Reveals(M,d) but either Signature(d) or Body(d) absent from ClientView(M)

laws.name: Export-view closure
laws.equation: Unresolved(ExportedView(M)) = {}, where Unresolved returns identifiers referenced by exported signatures or revealed bodies that are unavailable in the exported view.
laws.falsifier: exhibit module M with an exported signature or revealed body that references a name in Unresolved(ExportedView(M))

laws.name: Private-addition stability
laws.equation: PublicNames(AddPrivateHelper(M,h)) = PublicNames(M), where h is not named by M's explicit export set.
laws.falsifier: exhibit module M and unlisted helper h whose addition changes PublicNames(M), as with an unintended wildcard export

entries.breaker_note: Inspect the exported projection as if all hidden declarations were deleted: it must still resolve and type-check. Also test opacity, because a client proof that succeeds only by unfolding a provided body has crossed the module boundary.
entries.implementer_note: Use provides for signatures and specifications, reveals only when clients should unfold the definition, and list public names explicitly. Close the surface over every type, constructor, or imported module mentioned by exported material.

entries.title: Modular Specification of a Queue
data_structures: two-list queues with front and reversed rear
error_states: Empty maps to a nonempty abstract list, or another queue maps to the empty list while remaining unequal to Empty, making the Dequeue precondition unsound
Enqueue inserts x at the head of the abstract sequence instead of the tail, turning FIFO behavior into the wrong order
Dequeue returns the newest element from rear rather than the head element represented by the queue
Dequeue returns the correct head but its remainder drops, duplicates, or reorders the remaining abstract elements
the two-list implementation appends rear without reversing it, so Elements reports enqueued elements in reverse order

laws.name: Empty correctness and uniqueness
laws.equation: Elements(Empty()) = [] && (Elements(q) = [] => q = Empty()), where Elements maps a concrete queue to its abstract element list.
laws.falsifier: exhibit q with Elements(Empty()) != [] or with Elements(q) = [] and q != Empty()

laws.name: Enqueue abstraction law
laws.equation: Elements(Enqueue(q,x)) = Snoc(Elements(q),x), where Snoc(xs,x) appends x to the end of xs.
laws.falsifier: exhibit q,x with Elements(Enqueue(q,x)) != Snoc(Elements(q),x)

laws.name: Dequeue abstraction law
laws.equation: For q != Empty(), let (a,q2) = Dequeue(q): Cons(a,Elements(q2)) = Elements(q).
laws.falsifier: exhibit q,a,q2 with q != Empty(), (a,q2) = Dequeue(q), and Cons(a,Elements(q2)) != Elements(q)

laws.name: Two-list representation mapping
laws.equation: Elements(FQ(front,rear)) = Append(front,Reverse(rear)), where FQ is the private two-list queue representation.
laws.falsifier: exhibit front,rear with Elements(FQ(front,rear)) != Append(front,Reverse(rear))

entries.breaker_note: Write tests against Elements, not hidden front/rear fields, and use the operation equations from 9.3.1 as the public oracle. Add the 9.3.3 empty-uniqueness case because abstract emptiness must justify the concrete q != Empty() precondition.
entries.implementer_note: Choose Elements first, state operation correctness as extrinsic lemmas, and export those lemmas with the opaque type and operations. For 9.3.4's two-list implementation, discharge every law through Elements(q) = front ++ Reverse(rear), proving only the empty representation canonical.

entries.title: Equality-Supporting Types
error_states: compiled code compares possibly infinite sets or functions, requiring an equality computation that may not terminate or be computable
the exported Queue<A> claims compiled equality for every A even though its stored lists require equality support from A
IsEmpty returns false for Empty or true for a nonempty queue, so TryDequeue takes the wrong branch
a client uses representation equality as abstract queue equality and reports two queues unequal even though they represent the same element list
a compiled Length-based emptiness test disagrees with q == Empty(), permitting Dequeue on an abstractly empty queue or returning the default for a nonempty one

laws.name: Equality context boundary
laws.equation: EqAllowed(ghost,T) = true for every type T, and EqAllowed(compiled,T) = CompiledEq(T), where CompiledEq marks types with computable finite equality.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a compiled equality expression over type T with CompiledEq(T) = false that is nevertheless accepted

laws.name: Queue equality support follows its element type
laws.equation: CompiledEq(Queue<A>) = CompiledEq(A) for the two-list Queue representation, because equality of both stored lists requires equality of A.
laws.falsifier: exhibit element type A with CompiledEq(A) = false but CompiledEq(Queue<A>) = true

laws.name: Compiled emptiness agrees with Empty
laws.equation: For every q: IsEmpty(q) <=> q == Empty(), where IsEmpty is the exported compiled predicate and the equality in the contract is ghost equality.
laws.falsifier: exhibit q with IsEmpty(q) != (q == Empty())

laws.name: Abstract queue equality
laws.equation: AbsEq(q1,q2) <=> Elements(q1) = Elements(q2), where AbsEq means equality of represented queue contents; concrete q1 == q2 is not a substitute except for the unique empty representation.
laws.falsifier: exhibit q1,q2 with Elements(q1) = Elements(q2) but a client-defined AbsEq based on q1 == q2 returns false

laws.name: Length-based emptiness
laws.equation: For every q: Length(q) = 0 <=> q == Empty(), provided Length(q) = ListLength(Elements(q)) and Empty is the unique representation of the empty list.
laws.falsifier: exhibit q with Length(q) = 0 and q != Empty(), or Length(q) != 0 and q == Empty()

entries.breaker_note: Separate ghost equality from executable equality, and parameterize the latter by the element type's equality support. For queues, test the narrow compiled predicate from 9.4.2 rather than assuming concrete equality captures abstract contents.
entries.implementer_note: In 9.4.1, expose Queue(==)<A(==)> through an equality-supporting type synonym only when full compiled equality is intended. Otherwise follow 9.4.2: keep Queue opaque and export IsEmpty with IsEmpty(q) <=> q == Empty().

entries.title: Summary
error_states: a client proof unfolds a private queue representation, so replacing the two-list implementation breaks the client despite an unchanged public contract
an operation changes concrete state without preserving its abstraction-function equation, so the client observes abstract behavior outside the specification
an export uses provides where the client must unfold a definition, or reveals where the body was meant to remain a replaceable secret

laws.name: Representation-independent client proof
laws.equation: If implementations I1 and I2 have the same exported signatures, specifications, and revealed bodies, then ProvableClientFacts(C,I1) = ProvableClientFacts(C,I2) for every client C using only that exported view.
laws.falsifier: exhibit implementations I1,I2 with the same exported view and a client C whose proof succeeds for one only because it accesses an unexported representation detail

laws.name: Abstraction-operation commutation
laws.equation: For each concrete operation opC there is an abstract operation opA such that Abs(opC(c,x)) = opA(Abs(c),x), where Abs is the module's abstraction function; EnqueueCorrect and DequeueCorrect instantiate this pattern.
laws.falsifier: exhibit concrete state c and input x with Abs(opC(c,x)) != opA(Abs(c),x)

entries.breaker_note: Demand both opacity and commutation: clients must not see the module's secret, and every exported operation must have the promised effect after abstraction. A body revealed unnecessarily weakens the representation-change test.
entries.implementer_note: Make the abstraction function the bridge between private data and public specifications. Export signatures with provides by default, reveal only definitions intentionally used in client reasoning, and prove each concrete operation commutes with its abstract counterpart.

entries.title: Priority-Queue Specification
error_states: Empty returns a queue whose Elements value is not multiset{}
IsEmpty(pq) disagrees with Elements(pq) == multiset{}
Insert(pq,y) loses or duplicates an existing element — Elements(Insert(pq,y)) != Elements(pq) + multiset{y}
RemoveMin returns y that is not minimal — IsMin(y, Elements(pq)) is false
RemoveMin removes more or fewer than one occurrence — Elements(pq') + multiset{y} != Elements(pq)

laws.name: Empty abstraction
laws.equation: Elements(Empty()) == multiset{}
laws.falsifier: exhibit a queue pq with pq == Empty() and Elements(pq) != multiset{}

laws.name: Emptiness characterization
laws.equation: IsEmpty(pq) <==> Elements(pq) == multiset{}, where pq:PQueue
laws.falsifier: exhibit pq with IsEmpty(pq) != (Elements(pq) == multiset{})

laws.name: Insertion abstraction
laws.equation: Elements(Insert(pq,y)) == Elements(pq) + multiset{y}, where pq:PQueue and y:int
laws.falsifier: exhibit pq,y with Elements(Insert(pq,y)) != Elements(pq) + multiset{y}

laws.name: Minimum-removal contract
laws.equation: !IsEmpty(pq) && RemoveMin(pq) == (y,pq') => IsMin(y, Elements(pq)) && Elements(pq') + multiset{y} == Elements(pq), where pq':PQueue
laws.falsifier: exhibit nonempty pq with RemoveMin(pq) == (y,pq') and either !IsMin(y, Elements(pq)) or Elements(pq') + multiset{y} != Elements(pq)

laws.name: IsMin semantics
laws.equation: IsMin(y,s) <==> y in s && forall x, (x in s => y <= x), where s:multiset<int> and x,y:int
laws.falsifier: exhibit s,y with IsMin(y,s) true but some x in s has y > x

entries.breaker_note: Turn the abstract priority-queue contract into red tests for emptiness, insertion, and minimum removal, including both minimum selection and exact multiset conservation (10.0.0).
entries.implementer_note: Reason through Elements rather than a concrete representation, and keep the export boundary clear: clients use the provided operations and correctness lemmas while IsMin is the revealed helper (10.0.0-10.0.1).

entries.title: Designing the Data Structure
error_states: A Leaf/Node-shaped tree violates heap order — a node value x is greater than a value in its subtree, although the skeleton type accepts it
A tree violates Braun balance — for a Node, |Elements(left)| is neither |Elements(right)| nor |Elements(right)| + 1
Insert or RemoveMin returns pq' with !Valid(pq'), so the next operation starts from a broken representation
A correctness lemma is applied without Valid(pq), so it certifies an abstract result for a tree whose heap or balance assumptions do not hold

laws.name: Invariant decomposition
laws.equation: Valid(pq) <==> IsBinaryHeap(pq) && IsBalanced(pq), where pq:PQueue
laws.falsifier: exhibit pq with Valid(pq) true but either !IsBinaryHeap(pq) or !IsBalanced(pq)

laws.name: Braun balance
laws.equation: IsBalanced(Node(x,left,right)) => (|Elements(left)| == |Elements(right)| || |Elements(left)| == |Elements(right)| + 1)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a purported balanced Node(x,left,right) with |Elements(left)| < |Elements(right)| or |Elements(left)| > |Elements(right)| + 1

laws.name: Empty validity
laws.equation: Valid(Empty())
laws.falsifier: exhibit Empty() with !Valid(Empty())

laws.name: Insert preserves validity
laws.equation: Valid(pq) => Valid(Insert(pq,y)), where pq:PQueue and y:int
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid pq,y with !Valid(Insert(pq,y))

laws.name: RemoveMin preserves validity
laws.equation: Valid(pq) && !IsEmpty(pq) && RemoveMin(pq) == (y,pq') => Valid(pq'), where pq':PQueue
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid nonempty pq with RemoveMin(pq) == (y,pq') and !Valid(pq')

entries.breaker_note: Treat Valid as a gate, not as a comment: every produced tree must satisfy heap order and Braun balance, and every correctness claim must be conditional on it (10.1.0).
entries.implementer_note: Define the PQueue skeleton as Leaf/Node, then make Valid cover the non-skeletal constraints and carry it through Empty, Insert, and RemoveMin proofs.

entries.title: Implementation
error_states: Elements(Node(x,left,right)) omits or duplicates a payload — it does not equal multiset{x} + Elements(left) + Elements(right)
Insert returns a tree with wrong abstract contents or violates the heap or Braun invariant
RemoveMin returns the root but the returned value is not minimal — IsMin(y, Elements(pq)) is false
DeleteMin leaves a result with the wrong multiset or with child sizes outside Braun balance
ReplaceRoot fails to exchange exactly the old root for y, changing the multiset cardinality or element counts

laws.name: Structural Elements recursion
laws.equation: Elements(Leaf) == multiset{}; Elements(Node(x,left,right)) == multiset{x} + Elements(left) + Elements(right), where x:int and left,right:BraunTree
laws.falsifier: exhibit t with Elements(t) != the recursive union of every payload in t

laws.name: Heap root is subtree minimum
laws.equation: IsBinaryHeap(Node(x,left,right)) && z in Elements(Node(x,left,right)) => x <= z, where z:int
laws.falsifier: exhibit t == Node(5,Node(3,Leaf,Leaf),Leaf) with IsBinaryHeap(t) true and 5 > 3

laws.name: Insert correctness
laws.equation: Valid(pq) => Valid(Insert(pq,y)) && Elements(Insert(pq,y)) == Elements(pq) + multiset{y}, where y:int
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid pq,y with either !Valid(Insert(pq,y)) or Elements(Insert(pq,y)) != Elements(pq) + multiset{y}

laws.name: DeleteMin removes exactly the root
laws.equation: Valid(pq) && pq != Leaf && DeleteMin(pq) == pq' => Valid(pq') && Elements(pq') + multiset{root(pq)} == Elements(pq) && |Elements(pq')| == |Elements(pq)| - 1, where root(Node(x,left,right)) == x
laws.falsifier: exhibit nonleaf valid pq with DeleteMin(pq) == pq' and either the multiset equality or size decrement false

laws.name: ReplaceRoot exchange and size
laws.equation: Valid(pq) && pq != Leaf && ReplaceRoot(pq,y) == pq' => Valid(pq') && Elements(pq) + multiset{y} == Elements(pq') + multiset{root(pq)} && |Elements(pq')| == |Elements(pq)|
laws.falsifier: exhibit nonleaf valid pq,y with ReplaceRoot(pq,y) == pq' and an element exchange, validity, or size equality false

laws.name: RemoveMin correctness
laws.equation: Valid(pq) && !IsEmpty(pq) && RemoveMin(pq) == (y,pq') => IsMin(y, Elements(pq)) && Valid(pq') && Elements(pq') + multiset{y} == Elements(pq)
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid nonempty pq with RemoveMin(pq) == (y,pq') and either y is not minimal, pq' is invalid, or the multiset conservation equality fails

entries.breaker_note: Target structural omissions, wrong promotion, size imbalance, and multiset rearrangement errors; the crucial oracles are Elements, root minimality, and exact one-element removal (10.2.0-10.2.5).
entries.implementer_note: Use structural induction for operations and lemmas; in multiset branches, name subexpressions, assert extensional equalities, and expose associativity and commutativity rearrangements in calc steps (10.2.4-10.2.5).

entries.title: Making Intrinsic from Extrinsic
error_states: DeleteMin with only !IsEmpty as a precondition reaches pq.left.x when pq.left == Leaf — member access fails on a non-Braun tree
RemoveMin does not propagate Valid to its call of optimized DeleteMin — an invalid or unbalanced tree reaches the optimized branch
The intrinsic wrapper returns a result different from PriorityQueueExtrinsic for the same valid input
The intrinsic wrapper advertises a postcondition that is false — for example, the result is not Valid or the removed value is not minimal

laws.name: Balanced-tree leaf implication
laws.equation: IsBalanced(Node(x,left,right)) && left == Leaf => right == Leaf
laws.falsifier: exhibit t == Node(x,Leaf,Node(z,Leaf,Leaf)) with IsBalanced(t) true

laws.name: Optimized DeleteMin precondition
laws.equation: Valid(pq) && !IsEmpty(pq) => PreDeleteMin(pq), where PreDeleteMin(pq) := IsBalanced(pq) && !IsEmpty(pq)
laws.falsifier: exhibit pq with Valid(pq) && !IsEmpty(pq) but !PreDeleteMin(pq)

laws.name: Intrinsic-extrinsic operation equivalence
laws.equation: PriorityQueue.Op(args) == PriorityQueueExtrinsic.Op(args) for each exported Op in {Empty, IsEmpty, Insert, RemoveMin}
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid args and an exported Op whose public result differs from the extrinsic result

laws.name: Intrinsic RemoveMin postcondition
laws.equation: Valid(pq) && !IsEmpty(pq) && PriorityQueue.RemoveMin(pq) == (y,pq') => Valid(pq') && IsMin(y, Elements(pq)) && Elements(pq') + multiset{y} == Elements(pq)
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid nonempty pq with the public RemoveMin result violating validity, minimality, or conservation

entries.breaker_note: Add a red case for the optimized DeleteMin precondition: nonempty alone must not permit left.x access, and the strengthened Valid requirement must reach exported callers (10.3.0-10.3.1).
entries.implementer_note: Propagate the smallest invariant needed for safe code, then layer an intrinsically specified public module over the extrinsic implementation and discharge each wrapper contract by calling its proof lemma (10.3.1-10.3.2).

entries.title: Summary
error_states: An operation returns a skeleton that is not Valid even though its input is Valid — later clients inherit a broken heap or balance representation
The Elements abstraction disagrees with an operation's concrete effect — clients observe the wrong contents
Valid is true for a tree that fails the heap or balance property — a proof relies on an invariant fact that is not actually guaranteed
A client obtains a PQueue skeleton outside the exported-operation closure and uses it as if it were valid, bypassing the module's invariant boundary

laws.name: Invariant entails representation facts
laws.equation: Valid(pq) => IsBinaryHeap(pq) && IsBalanced(pq), where pq:PQueue
laws.falsifier: exhibit pq with Valid(pq) true and either heap order or Braun balance false

laws.name: Exported-operation closure
laws.equation: Valid(Empty()) && (Valid(pq) => Valid(Insert(pq,y))) && (Valid(pq) && !IsEmpty(pq) && RemoveMin(pq) == (y,pq') => Valid(pq'))
laws.falsifier: exhibit a value obtainable through the exported operations with !Valid(pq)

laws.name: Abstract insertion effect
laws.equation: Elements(Insert(pq,y)) == Elements(pq) + multiset{y}
laws.falsifier: exhibit pq,y with the insertion equality false

laws.name: Abstract minimum-removal effect
laws.equation: Valid(pq) && !IsEmpty(pq) && RemoveMin(pq) == (y,pq') => IsMin(y, Elements(pq)) && Elements(pq') + multiset{y} == Elements(pq)
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid nonempty pq with a nonminimal y or failed multiset conservation

entries.breaker_note: Use the summary as a closure test: Valid must imply the claimed representation facts, operations must preserve it, and Elements must describe their abstract effects.
entries.implementer_note: Choose an opaque Valid predicate plus an Elements abstraction, state them in preconditions and postconditions, and prove every invariant-derived property as a lemma from Valid (10.4).

entries.title: Loop Specifications
error_states: loop is entered at x == 3 with invariant x % 2 == 0 — the entry obligation is false even if the guard is already false
loop with guard i < 100 and invariant true exits at i == 101 — !guard holds but the claimed postcondition i == 100 does not
quotient-modulus loop exits with 7*x + y == 191 but y < 0 — the relation holds while x == 191/7 and y == 191%7 fails
square-root loop started with N == 104 but exits with r == 2 and N == 5 — the final bounds hold for a modified N, not the input

laws.name: loop-entry admissibility
laws.equation: Pre(s) => J(s), where s is the entry state and J is the loop invariant
laws.falsifier: exhibit s with Pre(s) && !J(s)

laws.name: abstract loop exit
laws.equation: Run(s0) = s1 && J(s0) => J(s1) && !B(s1), where B is the guard
laws.falsifier: exhibit s0,s1 with Run(s0) = s1 && J(s0) && (!J(s1) || B(s1))

laws.name: postcondition adequacy
laws.equation: forall s. J(s) && !B(s) => Q(s), where Q is the required postcondition
laws.falsifier: exhibit s with J(s) && !B(s) && !Q(s)

laws.name: frame stability
laws.equation: v notin Frame(Run) => v(s1) = v(s0), where Run(s0) = s1
laws.falsifier: exhibit s0,s1,v with Run(s0) = s1 && v notin Frame(Run) && v(s1) != v(s0)

entries.breaker_note: Use the entry, exit, and post-adequacy obligations from 11.0.1 and 11.0.3; add an explicit stability test for every value that the result is meant to retain, as exposed by 11.0.5.
entries.implementer_note: Choose J so initialization proves it and J && !B proves the postcondition; relational invariants from 11.0.4 and a deliberate frame prevent correct-looking results about the wrong state.

entries.title: Loop Implementations
error_states: quotient body changes x without the compensating change to y — 7*x + y is no longer 191 after one iteration
two-step quotient update uses x' == x + 2 and y' == y - 14 when 7 <= y < 14 — the equation is preserved but y' becomes negative
sum loop increments n but leaves s unchanged — at n == 1 and s == 0 it reaches n' == 2 and s' == 0 instead of s' == 1
loop body accidentally assigns a, which was supposed to remain equal to input X — inferred framing no longer supports a == X

laws.name: invariant preservation
laws.equation: J(s) && B(s) && Body(s) = s' => J(s')
laws.falsifier: exhibit s,s' with J(s) && B(s) && Body(s) = s' && !J(s')

laws.name: quotient-state preservation
laws.falsifier: exhibit x,y,x',y' satisfying the antecedent with y' < 0 || 7*x' + y' != 191

laws.name: triangular-sum step
laws.falsifier: exhibit n,s,n',s' satisfying the step premises with s' != n'*(n'-1)/2

laws.name: inferred local frame
laws.equation: v notin Assigned(Body) && Body(s) = s' => v(s') = v(s)
laws.falsifier: exhibit Body,s,s',v with v notin Assigned(Body) && Body(s) = s' && v(s') != v(s)

entries.breaker_note: Test one body step from J && B, not a sampled number of repetitions (11.1.1). Include boundary states such as 7 <= y < 14 from 11.1.0 and stability checks derived from the assigned-variable set in 11.1.3.
entries.implementer_note: Work backward through assignments by substitution, and strengthen J when the one-step obligation needs a fact not already present. For derived accumulators, use the algebraic recurrence as in 11.1.2.

entries.title: Loop Termination
error_states: body does nothing — it preserves every invariant but leaves the termination metric unchanged and can loop forever
quotient body updates x' == x - 1 and y' == y + 7 — 7*x + y is preserved while guard 7 <= y remains true forever
chosen integer metric is negative at the back edge — ordinary decrease is not a well-founded termination argument
default metric F - E for guard E < F stays constant or increases on a body branch — that branch has no proved progress

laws.name: integer ranking decrease
laws.equation: J(s) && B(s) && Body(s) = s' => D(s') < D(s) && 0 <= D(s), where D is the integer decreases expression
laws.falsifier: exhibit s,s' with J(s) && B(s) && Body(s) = s' && (D(s') >= D(s) || D(s) < 0)

laws.name: eventual guard falsification
laws.equation: J(s[0]) && Body terminates && every guarded step satisfies D(s[k+1]) < D(s[k]) && 0 <= D(s[k]) => exists k >= 0. J(s[k]) && !B(s[k])
laws.falsifier: exhibit an infinite guarded execution satisfying J and all stated ranking premises

laws.name: quotient progress
laws.falsifier: exhibit y,y' with y >= 7 && y' = y - 7 && (y' >= y || y < 0)

laws.name: default comparison metrics
laws.equation: B = (E < F) => D = F-E; B = (E <= F) => D = F-E; B = (E != F) => D = abs(F-E)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a guarded body step for which the selected D does not satisfy D' < D && 0 <= D

entries.breaker_note: Attack every branch at the back edge with the ranking equation, especially invariant-preserving reverse updates from 11.2.0. Treat the defaults in 11.2.1 as candidates that still must decrease.
entries.implementer_note: Snapshot D before the body and prove a strict well-founded decrease afterward. If preservation succeeds but progress fails, redesign the body or supply a better decreases expression.

entries.title: Summarizing the Loop Rule
error_states: caller enters the loop with J false — the loop summary is used outside its precondition
body decreases D but destroys J — termination is shown while partial correctness is lost
body preserves J but leaves D unchanged — partial correctness is shown while termination is lost
caller asserts Q after the loop even though some state satisfies J && !B && !Q — the summary is too weak for Q

laws.name: loop-use rule
laws.equation: {J} Loop(B,J,D,Body) {J && !B}
laws.falsifier: exhibit an execution admitted from J that exits with !J || B

laws.name: combined body obligation
laws.equation: J(s) && B(s) && Body(s) = s' => J(s') && D(s') <_wf D(s), where <_wf is the chosen well-founded order
laws.falsifier: exhibit s,s' with J(s) && B(s) && Body(s) = s' and either !J(s') or !(D(s') <_wf D(s))

laws.name: client consequence
laws.equation: (forall s. J(s) && !B(s) => Q(s)) => {J} Loop(B,J,D,Body) {Q}
laws.falsifier: exhibit s with J(s) && !B(s) && !Q(s)

entries.breaker_note: The packet should contain two independent red-test families: client use of J && !B, and one-step implementation of J plus decreasing D.
entries.implementer_note: Discharge the loop in three cuts: establish J, prove Body maps J && B back to J while decreasing D, then derive the requested postcondition from J && !B.

entries.title: Integer Square Root
error_states: SquareRoot(104) returns r == 9 — r*r <= 104 holds but 104 < (r+1)*(r+1) fails
SquareRoot(104) returns r == 11 — the successor bound holds but r*r <= 104 fails
optimized loop initializes s to 0 instead of 1 — s no longer represents (r+1)*(r+1)
optimized update uses the wrong increment for s — guard s <= N diverges from the original square comparison and exits at the wrong r

laws.name: integer-square-root characterization
laws.equation: SquareRoot(N) = r => r*r <= N && N < (r+1)*(r+1), where N and r are natural numbers
laws.falsifier: exhibit N,r with SquareRoot(N) = r && (r*r > N || N >= (r+1)*(r+1))

laws.name: cached-square representation
laws.falsifier: exhibit an initial cache s0 != 1 or a step satisfying the premises with s' != (r'+1)*(r'+1)

laws.name: guard substitution
laws.falsifier: exhibit N,r,s with s = (r+1)*(r+1) and different truth values for s <= N and (r+1)*(r+1) <= N

entries.breaker_note: Split the postcondition into both inequalities and test each independently (11.4.0). For the optimized program, make the cached-square representation and guard equivalence separate laws (11.4.1).
entries.implementer_note: Use one desired conjunct as J and the negation of the other as B. When programming by wishing, initialize the wished-for quantity and derive its update by weakest-precondition algebra.

entries.title: Summary
error_states: loop invariant is not established before the first guard check — the implementation starts outside its specified state space
one body branch fails to re-establish the invariant — a later exit can violate the advertised result
all body branches preserve the invariant but one fails to decrease the metric — the loop can diverge
an unframed local changes during the loop — the client observes a value that the loop summary treated as stable

laws.name: three-part loop specification
laws.equation: Spec(Loop) = (B,J,F), where B is the guard, J the invariant, and F the frame
laws.falsifier: exhibit a loop whose claimed client result depends on a guard, invariant, or frame fact absent from Spec(Loop)

laws.name: total loop correctness
laws.equation: Pre(s0) => J(s0); J(s) && B(s) && Body(s) = s' => J(s') && D(s') <_wf D(s); loop exit s1 => J(s1) && !B(s1)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a loop violating initialization, one-step preservation, strict decrease, or the exit summary

laws.name: frame agreement
laws.equation: v notin F && Loop(s0) = s1 => v(s1) = v(s0)
laws.falsifier: exhibit s0,s1,v with Loop(s0) = s1 && v notin F && v(s1) != v(s0)

entries.breaker_note: Use this section as the minimum loop battery: initialization, one-step preservation, strict progress, exit adequacy, and frame agreement.
entries.implementer_note: Keep loop use separate from loop implementation: clients reason only from J, !B, and the frame, while the body is discharged once from J && B.

entries.title: Iterative Fibonacci
error_states: iterative method returns a value other than Fib(n) — the efficient implementation disagrees with the recursive specification
x and y are updated sequentially using the new x — y becomes 2*old_y instead of old_x + old_y
invariant uses y == Fib(i-1) at i == 0 without a guard — it demands the undefined call Fib(-1)
loop index leaves 0 <= i <= n or skips n — termination or the substitution of n for i at exit fails
body increments i but does not advance the Fibonacci pair — x still denotes Fib(i-1) after the step

laws.name: Fibonacci equations
laws.falsifier: exhibit k with a returned Fib value that violates its applicable base or recurrence equation

laws.name: consecutive-pair step
laws.falsifier: exhibit i,x,y,x',y',i' satisfying the step premises with x' != Fib(i') || y' != Fib(i'+1)

laws.name: iterative refinement
laws.equation: ComputeFib(n) = Fib(n)
laws.falsifier: exhibit n with ComputeFib(n) != Fib(n)

laws.name: index progress and definedness
laws.falsifier: exhibit n,i,i' violating the range or decrease, or exhibit an invariant call Fib(k) with k < 0

entries.breaker_note: Compare the iterative result to the recursive oracle and test the simultaneous pair transition, especially n == 0 and n == 1. The design warning about Fib(i-1) is a definedness test, not style.
entries.implementer_note: Apply replace-constant-by-variable: maintain x == Fib(i) until i == n, then add the adjacent value y == Fib(i+1) so the recurrence supplies the next state.

entries.title: Fibonacci Squared
error_states: initial state uses y != 1 or k != 0 — the wished-for square and cross-term invariants fail before the loop
update for y omits k — the next Fibonacci square loses the cross term 2*Fib(n)*Fib(n+1)
updates are sequential and k reads the new y — the recurrence uses mixed generations and drifts from the specification
compiled body performs multiplication — it violates the stated addition-only implementation constraint even if the numeric answer is right
loop exits with x != Fib(N)*Fib(N) — the wishes were maintained for the wrong index or not maintained at all

laws.name: squared-Fibonacci state recurrence
laws.falsifier: exhibit n and a candidate base or transition tuple that differs from the stated tuple

laws.name: SquareFib refinement
laws.equation: SquareFib(N) = Fib(N)*Fib(N)
laws.falsifier: exhibit N with SquareFib(N) != Fib(N)*Fib(N)

laws.name: addition-only execution
laws.equation: runtime_mul_count(SquareFib,N) = 0, counting only compiled operations and excluding ghost specifications
laws.falsifier: exhibit N and an executed multiplication in the non-ghost SquareFib trace

entries.breaker_note: Test the three-component recurrence as one simultaneous transition (12.1.1-12.1.2), plus the independent no-runtime-multiplication constraint.
entries.implementer_note: Record each wish as an invariant, solve its base value, expand Fib algebraically in calc steps, and commit the coupled updates simultaneously so every right-hand side reads the old state.

entries.title: Powers of 2
error_states: ComputePower(0) initializes p to 2 — the loop may do no iterations and returns 2 instead of Power(0) == 1
body increments i without doubling p — p remains Power(i-1) after the step
initial index is changed to 1 without handling n == 0 — 0 <= i <= n fails and guard i != n can move away from n
what-is-left invariant omits the bound i <= n — n-i no longer denotes the intended remaining exponent

laws.name: power equations
laws.equation: Power(0) = 1; k >= 0 => Power(k+1) = 2*Power(k)
laws.falsifier: exhibit k with a returned Power value violating the base or successor equation

laws.name: what-has-been-done step
laws.equation: p = Power(i) && p' = 2*p && i' = i+1 => p' = Power(i')
laws.falsifier: exhibit p,i,p',i' satisfying the step premises with p' != Power(i')

laws.name: what-is-left conservation
laws.equation: 0 <= i < n && p*Power(n-i) = Power(n) && p' = 2*p && i' = i+1 => p'*Power(n-i') = Power(n)
laws.falsifier: exhibit n,i,p,p',i' satisfying the premises with p'*Power(n-i') != Power(n)

laws.name: power-loop refinement
laws.equation: ComputePower(n) = Power(n)
laws.falsifier: exhibit n with ComputePower(n) != Power(n)

entries.breaker_note: Exercise both invariant styles from 12.2.0-12.2.1 at boundary n == 0 and across one step; both must refine the same Power function.
entries.implementer_note: Use p == Power(i) when the recurrence advances naturally, or conserve p*Power(n-i) == Power(n) when the remaining-work view aligns better; keep 0 <= i <= n in either design.

entries.title: Sums
error_states: recursive sum includes F(hi) or omits F(lo) — it no longer represents the half-open range lo <= i < hi
upward loop increments i before adding F(i) — it omits F(lo) and may include F(hi)
downward loop adds F(i) before decrementing i — it includes F(hi) and omits F(lo)
LoopUp uses s == SumUp(lo,i) but supplies no upper-extension lemma — the body cannot re-establish the invariant
recursive function or lemma keeps width hi-lo unchanged on a branch — the recursion has no proved termination

laws.name: half-open recursive folds
laws.equation: SU(lo,lo) = 0; lo < hi => SU(lo,hi) = F(lo)+SU(lo+1,hi); SD(lo,lo) = 0; lo < hi => SD(lo,hi) = SD(lo,hi-1)+F(hi-1)
laws.falsifier: exhibit F,lo,hi where SU or SD violates its applicable base or recursive equation

laws.name: direction-independent sum
laws.equation: lo <= hi => SU(lo,hi) = SD(lo,hi)
laws.falsifier: exhibit F,lo,hi with lo <= hi && SU(lo,hi) != SD(lo,hi)

laws.name: upper and lower extension
laws.equation: lo < hi => SU(lo,hi-1)+F(hi-1) = SU(lo,hi) && F(lo)+SD(lo+1,hi) = SD(lo,hi)
laws.falsifier: exhibit F,lo,hi with lo < hi and either extension equality false

laws.name: iterative sum refinement
laws.equation: lo <= hi => LoopUp(lo,hi) = LoopDown(lo,hi) = SU(lo,hi) = SD(lo,hi)
laws.falsifier: exhibit F,lo,hi with lo <= hi and one loop result unequal to SU(lo,hi) or SD(lo,hi)

laws.name: interval-width decrease
laws.equation: w = hi-lo; every recursive call uses w' with 0 <= w' < w
laws.falsifier: exhibit a non-base recursive branch with w' >= w || w' < 0

entries.breaker_note: Use an arbitrary F that makes endpoint mistakes visible, then compare both recursive definitions and both loop directions. Require the append/prepend equalities from 12.3.0 and 12.3.2, not just a few numeric examples.
entries.implementer_note: For LoopUp, either use SumDown directly, call AppendSumUp, or conserve s + SumUp(i,hi); use the dual choices for LoopDown. Preserve post-increment upward and pre-decrement downward ordering (12.3.3).

entries.title: Summary
error_states: iteration direction and recursive unfolding direction disagree with no bridge lemma — the chosen invariant is not preserved
upward loop consumes F(i+1) instead of F(i) — its result shifts the half-open range by one
downward loop consumes F(i) before decrementing — it includes the excluded upper endpoint and misses the lower endpoint

laws.name: recursive-iterative agreement
laws.equation: IterUp(lo,hi) = IterDown(lo,hi) = RecUp(lo,hi) = RecDown(lo,hi)
laws.falsifier: exhibit F,lo,hi with lo <= hi and any two of the four results unequal

laws.name: index-consumption order
laws.equation: UpStep(s,i) = (s+F(i),i+1); DownStep(s,i) = (s+F(i-1),i-1)
laws.falsifier: exhibit an upward step that consumes an index other than old i or a downward step that consumes an index other than old i-1

laws.name: direction bridge
laws.equation: RecUp(lo,hi) = RecDown(lo,hi), so either recursive orientation may specify either loop orientation when this equality is available
laws.falsifier: exhibit F,lo,hi with lo <= hi && RecUp(lo,hi) != RecDown(lo,hi)

entries.breaker_note: Demand extensional agreement across both recursion and iteration directions, with endpoint-sensitive tests rather than commutative examples that hide ordering errors.
entries.implementer_note: Align the invariant with the recurrence that unfolds at the index being consumed; if directions differ, introduce the exact bridge lemma instead of weakening the invariant.

entries.title: About Arrays
error_states: An access uses i < 0 or i >= a.Length and reads or writes an element instead of failing the bounds obligation.
A point update a[i] := v changes a[j] for i != j, or two equal index expressions are incorrectly treated as distinct cells.
var b := a is treated as a deep copy, so writing b[i] leaves a[i] unchanged.
A captured sequence s := a[..] changes after a is mutated, or a slice has the wrong endpoints or length.

laws.name: Index validity and array snapshot length
laws.equation: validIndex(a,i) iff 0 <= i && i < len(a); len(a[..]) == len(a) (len(a)=a.Length)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a with len(a)=3 and i=3 where a[i] is accepted, or a[..] has length other than 3

laws.name: Point-update locality
laws.equation: write(a,i,v)[j] == (if j == i then v else a[j]) for validIndex(a,i)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a,i,j,v with i != j and write(a,i,v)[j] != a[j]

laws.name: Reference alias visibility
laws.equation: a == b && write(b,i,v) => a[i] == v (a and b are the same array reference)
laws.falsifier: exhibit b := a and a write through b such that the observed a[i] != v

laws.name: Immutable sequence snapshot
laws.equation: s := a[..]; write(a,i,v) => s == old(a[..]) and s[i] == old(a[i])
laws.falsifier: exhibit a,i,v where s := a[..] and after write(a,i,v), s[i] != old(a[i])

laws.name: Half-open slice splitting
laws.equation: 0 <= lo <= mid <= hi <= |s| => s[lo..mid] + s[mid..hi] == s[lo..hi] (|s|=sequence length)
laws.falsifier: exhibit s,lo,mid,hi in range with s[lo..mid] + s[mid..hi] != s[lo..hi]

entries.breaker_note: Use bounds, point-update locality, alias visibility, and immutable snapshots as red tests. The slice-splitting law is the extensionality fact later proofs depend on (13.0.1-13.0.4).
entries.implementer_note: Treat arrays as heap references and sequences as values. Prove every index range before access, and use half-open slices as the stable mathematical view of array regions (13.0.0-13.0.4).

entries.title: Linear Search
error_states: The method returns n < 0 or n > a.Length, or evaluates P(a[n]) when n == a.Length.
The method returns a.Length even though some valid index i satisfies P(a[i]).
The method returns a later matching index while an earlier index j < n also satisfies P(a[j]).
The loop increments without a successful check or fails to decrease a.Length - n, so it can skip a match or fail to terminate.

laws.name: Search result contract
laws.falsifier: exhibit a with L=2 and an implementation result n=3, or n=2 while evaluating P(a[2])

laws.name: Defeat must be justified
laws.equation: n == L => forall i :: 0 <= i && i < L => !P(a[i])
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[4,7], P(x)=x==7, and an implementation returning n=L

laws.name: First-match guarantee
laws.equation: P(a[n]) => forall i :: 0 <= i && i < n => !P(a[i])
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[7,7], P(x)=x==7, and an implementation returning n=1

laws.name: Existential precondition forces success
laws.equation: (exists i :: 0 <= i && i < L && P(a[i])) => n < L && P(a[n])
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[7], P(x)=x==7, and an implementation returning n=L

laws.name: Quantifier range split
laws.equation: forall i :: 0 <= i && i < n+1 => !P(a[i]) iff (forall i :: 0 <= i && i < n => !P(a[i])) && !P(a[n])
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[7], n=0, P(x)=x==7, with the prefix condition true but the n+1 condition false

laws.name: Variant progress
laws.falsifier: exhibit a length L and a loop branch with n'=n, so L-n' == L-n

entries.breaker_note: Break the result contract, the no-match justification, firstness, and the existential-success implication. Also mutate the range split or the variant to catch an unchecked increment and nontermination (13.1.1-13.1.5).
entries.implementer_note: Use the index as a replace-constant-by-variable invariant; on each iteration preserve the already-ruled-out prefix and check the current element before advancing. With a known witness, switch to the invariant that a witness remains at or after n and supply decreases L-n (13.1.1, 13.1.4).

entries.title: Binary Search
error_states: An unsorted array is accepted, so the search discards a region that can contain the key.
The returned n leaves some i < n with a[i] >= key or some i >= n with a[i] < key, so it is not an insertion point.
A present key is reported absent, or the method returns a later occurrence instead of the leftmost insertion point.
A midpoint is outside the current window and is used for an invalid array access.
Replacing lo := mid + 1 with lo := mid leaves a one-element window unchanged and the loop does not terminate.

laws.name: Global sortedness
laws.equation: forall i,j :: 0 <= i && i < j && j < L => a[i] <= a[j] (L=len(a))
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[2,1] that is accepted as sorted, with i=0 and j=1 violating a[i] <= a[j]

laws.name: Earliest insertion partition
laws.equation: 0 <= n && n <= L && (forall i :: 0 <= i && i < n => a[i] < key) && (forall i :: n <= i && i < L => key <= a[i])
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[1,3], key=2, and n=0 or n=2

laws.name: Contains equivalence
laws.equation: (n < L && a[n] == key) iff (exists i :: 0 <= i && i < L && a[i] == key)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[1,2,2], key=2, with a search result n=3 or a[n] != key despite a matching element

laws.name: Midpoint lies in the window
laws.equation: lo < hi && mid=floor((lo+hi)/2) => lo <= mid && mid < hi
laws.falsifier: exhibit lo=0, hi=1 and a buggy midpoint mid=1, which is not a valid element of [lo,hi)

laws.name: Window strictly shrinks
laws.equation: if a[mid] < key then (lo',hi')=(mid+1,hi); else (lo',hi')=(lo,mid); in both cases hi'-lo' < hi-lo
laws.falsifier: exhibit lo=0, hi=1 with buggy then update lo'=mid=0, leaving hi'-lo' == hi-lo

entries.breaker_note: Test global sortedness, the two insertion partitions, Contains, midpoint bounds, and strict window shrinkage. The one-element-window mutation is the tight termination breaker (13.2.0-13.2.2).
entries.implementer_note: Maintain the two quantified exclusion regions around [lo,hi), and move the midpoint into exactly one region: lo=mid+1 when it is too small, hi=mid otherwise. Use the window width as the decreases measure (13.2.2).

entries.title: Minimum
error_states: The method returns a value below every array element but not equal to any element, such as an arbitrary uninitialized out-parameter.
Initialization m := a[0] is attempted on an empty array.
A smaller later element is ignored, so the returned m is greater than some a[i].
The loop exits with a valid lower bound but without preserving that m came from the array.

laws.name: Minimum lower bound
laws.equation: forall i :: 0 <= i && i < L => m <= a[i] (L=len(a))
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[2,10,1] and m=2, since m <= a[2] is false

laws.name: Minimum is an input
laws.equation: L != 0 => exists i :: 0 <= i && i < L && m == a[i]
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[2,10] and m=0, which is a lower bound but is not an array element

laws.name: Candidate update preserves the minimum
laws.equation: m' == (if a[n] < m then a[n] else m) => m' <= m && m' <= a[n]
laws.falsifier: exhibit m=10, a[n]=1, and an update producing m'=10

laws.name: Witness initialization requires nonempty input
laws.equation: L != 0 => exists i :: 0 <= i && i < L
laws.falsifier: exhibit L=0 with code attempting m := a[0]

entries.breaker_note: The red tests must distinguish a lower bound from an actual input minimum and must reject empty-array initialization. A valid implementation cannot lose a smaller later element (13.3.0-13.3.2).
entries.implementer_note: Start with a witnessed element, make the final witness postcondition an invariant, and update the candidate only when the next element is smaller. The added witness obligation exposes the needed nonempty precondition (13.3.1).

entries.title: Coincidence Count
error_states: Duplicates are counted as distinct values rather than by multiset intersection, so a=[1,1] and b=[1] incorrectly produce c=2.
An equal head increments c but fails to advance both indices, or advances an index without counting the equal pair.
When a[m] < b[n], the implementation advances the wrong side and can discard a remaining coincidence, such as a=[1,2], b=[2].
The loop exits with one tail empty while the residual tails still contribute to c, or a branch leaves the termination measure unchanged.

laws.name: Coincidence result
laws.equation: c == |M(a[..]) * M(b[..])| (M(s)=multiset(s), *=multiset intersection, |X|=cardinality)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[1,1], b=[1] with c=2 instead of 1

laws.name: What's-yet-to-be-done conservation
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[1], b=[1], and post-state c=0,m=1,n=1, giving 0 != 1

laws.name: Equal-head decomposition
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[1], b=[1], m=n=0 with the singleton term omitted, making cardinalities 1 and 0

laws.name: Advance the smaller head
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[1,2], b=[2], m=n=0, and advance n instead of m, yielding residual cardinality 0 instead of 1

laws.name: Tail exhaustion closes the proof
laws.falsifier: exhibit an exit state with m=len(a), n<len(b), but a nonempty tail for a or a nonzero residual intersection

laws.name: Termination measure decreases
laws.equation: V=len(a)-m + len(b)-n; every case gives V' < V
laws.falsifier: exhibit a branch with m'=m and n'=n, so V' == V

entries.breaker_note: Use multiset-preserving tests for duplicates, equal heads, and both smaller-head branches. The conservation law plus tail exhaustion catches dropped or unprocessed matches; the variant catches stalled branches (13.4.1-13.4.6).
entries.implementer_note: Write the residual-tail invariant first, then make each comparison case preserve it and reduce the sum of remaining lengths. When automation fails, isolate a branch with an assertion and discharge sequence extensionality, multiset distribution, and commutativity through focused lemmas (13.4.3-13.4.6).

entries.title: Slope Search
data_structures: key contour and shrinking search rectangle
error_states: The search moves in the wrong direction and skips a key that exists in the remaining rectangle.
A move leaves m or n outside the matrix bounds, causing the next a[m,n] access to be invalid.
The rectangle witness invariant is lost, so the loop can terminate without returning a cell equal to key.
The loop changes neither the row nor the column or uses a nondecreasing variant, so it can fail to terminate.

laws.name: Row and column monotonicity
laws.equation: (j < j' => a[i,j] <= a[i,j']) && (i < i' => a[i,j] <= a[i',j]) for valid row and column indices
laws.falsifier: exhibit a matrix and valid i,j,j' or i,i',j where a step East or South decreases the value

laws.name: Rectangle witness invariant
laws.falsifier: exhibit a state with valid m,n but no key in rows m..L0 and columns 0..n

laws.name: Less-than branch eliminates a row
laws.equation: a[m,n] < key => forall j :: 0 <= j && j <= n => a[m,j] < key
laws.falsifier: exhibit a[m,n] < key but some valid j <= n has a[m,j] >= key

laws.name: Greater-than branch eliminates a column
laws.equation: a[m,n] > key => forall i :: m <= i && i < L0 => a[i,n] > key
laws.falsifier: exhibit a[m,n] > key but some valid i >= m has a[i,n] <= key

laws.name: Variant progress and result
laws.equation: V=L0-m+n; m'=m+1 or n'=n-1 => V'=V-1; guard false => a[m,n] == key
laws.falsifier: exhibit a branch with no index change, or a guard-false state with a[m,n] != key

entries.breaker_note: Break monotonicity, the rectangle witness, either branch's elimination fact, and the row/column variant. Boundary moves are especially important because the next loop guard still indexes the matrix (13.5.0-13.5.1).
entries.implementer_note: Start at the upper-right corner so the remaining witness rectangle is the whole matrix, then move down when the current value is too small and left when it is too large. Keep proper-index bounds as an invariant and use L0-m+n as the decreasing measure (13.5.0-13.5.1).

entries.title: Canyon Search
error_states: The method accesses a[0] or b[0] when either input is empty.
It returns a distance not realized by any pair of input elements.
It misses a closer pair by advancing the wrong index, such as a=[0,100], b=[50,51], where the true minimum is 49.
It proves d is minimal only in the visited L-shaped region but exits while a closer pair remains in the unexplored corner.

laws.name: Absolute-distance algebra
laws.equation: Dist(x,y) == (if x < y then y-x else x-y); Dist(x,y) == Dist(y,x) && Dist(x,y) >= 0
laws.falsifier: exhibit x,y with Dist(x,y) != Dist(y,x), or a negative returned distance

laws.name: Minimum is attained
laws.equation: exists i,j :: 0 <= i && i < La && 0 <= j && j < Lb && d == Dist(a[i],b[j]) (La=len(a), Lb=len(b))
laws.falsifier: exhibit nonempty a,b and d not equal to Dist(a[i],b[j]) for any valid pair

laws.name: Global minimum lower bound
laws.equation: forall i,j :: 0 <= i && i < La && 0 <= j && j < Lb => d <= Dist(a[i],b[j])
laws.falsifier: exhibit a valid pair with Dist(a[i],b[j]) < d

laws.name: Frontier monotonicity
laws.equation: sorted(a) && sorted(b) && a[m] <= b[n] => forall j >= n: Dist(a[m],b[n]) <= Dist(a[m],b[j]); b[n] <= a[m] => forall i >= m: Dist(a[m],b[n]) <= Dist(a[i],b[n])
laws.falsifier: exhibit sorted arrays and a frontier comparison where an onward distance is smaller than the current frontier distance

laws.name: Weakened L-shaped invariant
laws.equation: forall i,j :: valid(i,j) => d <= Dist(a[i],b[j]) || (m <= i && n <= j)
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid i,j outside the excluded corner with Dist(a[i],b[j]) < d

laws.name: Minimum update and termination
laws.equation: d' == min(d,Dist(a[m],b[n])); V=La-m+Lb-n; every iteration gives d' <= d and V' < V
laws.falsifier: exhibit a current pair closer than d that is not incorporated, or a branch with V' == V

entries.breaker_note: Test attainedness separately from the lower-bound claim, then target the frontier direction with arrays where the closest pair is beyond one current index. The L-shaped invariant and decreasing sum catch premature exit and stalled scans (13.6.0-13.6.2).
entries.implementer_note: Initialize d from a real pair, weaken the universal postcondition over the unexplored corner, and update d before advancing one frontier. Sortedness tells which index can move without losing a possible minimum (13.6.1-13.6.2).

entries.title: Majority Vote
data_structures: ghost witnesses K, hasWinner, and w
Result datatype with NoWinner and Winner(Candidate)
error_states: Count has an off-by-one error and counts a[hi] or omits a[hi-1], so Count([x],0,1,x) is not 1.
The loop resets k or c without preserving c == Count(a,lo,hi,k), so it loses the true majority or returns a non-majority candidate.
The algorithm discards a prefix that still gives the true winner a strict majority, so the suffix no longer has the required winner.
Two distinct candidates are treated as strict-majority winners, or DetermineElection returns Winner(c) for a non-majority c or NoWinner when a majority exists.
An assign-such-that ghost witness is used without proving existence, or hi fails to advance and the scan does not terminate.

laws.name: Count recurrence
laws.equation: Count(a,lo,hi,x) == (if lo == hi then 0 else Count(a,lo,hi-1,x) + (if a[hi-1] == x then 1 else 0)) (Count counts a[lo..hi))
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[x], lo=0, hi=1 with Count(a,lo,hi,x) == 0

laws.name: Count split
laws.equation: 0 <= lo <= mid <= hi <= |a| => Count(a,lo,mid,x) + Count(a,mid,hi,x) == Count(a,lo,hi,x)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[x,y], lo=0, mid=1, hi=2 where the split sum differs from Count(a,0,2,x)

laws.name: Distinct-count bound
laws.equation: x != y => Count(a,lo,hi,x) + Count(a,lo,hi,y) <= hi-lo
laws.falsifier: exhibit distinct x,y and a[lo..hi] where the two counts sum to more than hi-lo

laws.name: Strict-majority uniqueness
laws.equation: HasMajority(a,lo,hi,x) && HasMajority(a,lo,hi,y) => x == y (HasMajority(a,p,q,x) iff q-p < 2*Count(a,p,q,x))
laws.falsifier: exhibit distinct x,y both reported as majority in the same interval

laws.name: Majority survives cancellation
laws.equation: HasMajority(a,lo,|a|,K) && 2*Count(a,lo,hi,K) <= hi-lo => HasMajority(a,hi,|a|,K)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a,lo,hi,K satisfying the antecedent but with |a|-hi >= 2*Count(a,hi,|a|,K)

laws.name: Candidate loop invariant
laws.equation: 0 <= lo <= hi <= |a| && c == Count(a,lo,hi,k) && HasMajority(a,lo,hi,k) && (hasWinner => HasMajority(a,lo,|a|,K))
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[A,B,A] and reset state lo=2,hi=3,k=A,c=0, where c != Count(a,2,3,A)

laws.name: Assign-such-that witness
laws.equation: assignSuchThat(P) succeeds => exists x :: P(x) and P(chosen)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a sequence with no K satisfying HasMajority(a,0,|a|,K) but attempt ghost K :| HasMajority(a,0,|a|,K)

laws.name: Election result exactness
laws.equation: result=Winner(c) => HasMajority(a,0,|a|,c); result=NoWinner => !exists c :: HasMajority(a,0,|a|,c)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a=[A,A,B] returning NoWinner or Winner(B)

laws.name: Scan progress
laws.equation: V=|a|-hi; every nonreturning loop branch has hi'=hi+1 and V'=V-1
laws.falsifier: exhibit a branch with hi'=hi, so V' == V

entries.breaker_note: Break Count and split arithmetic first, then target cancellation, candidate-state preservation, unique majority, and exact Winner/NoWinner results. Include a ghost-witness absence case and a stalled hi update (13.7.0-13.7.5).
entries.implementer_note: Build the proof around Count, SplitCount, and DistinctCounts; maintain a witnessed majority candidate over the active interval and preserve the whole-sequence winner through canceled prefixes. Use ghost values only to expose proof witnesses, then recheck the candidate at runtime before constructing Result (13.7.0-13.7.5).

entries.title: Simple Frames
error_states: method changes an existing array not named by its write frame — an unlisted location differs between the pre-state and post-state
increment specification uses old(a)[i] instead of old(a[i]) — it reads the post-state element rather than the entry value
factory returns an old aliased array while its caller treats the result as newly allocated — fresh(result) is false and a caller update smashes existing state
function reads an array outside its read frame — its result changes although the heaps agree on every declared dependency

laws.name: Write-frame confinement
laws.equation: ChangedExisting(H,H') subseteq M, where H and H' are the pre/post heaps, M is the modifies set evaluated in H, and ChangedExisting contains pre-existing objects whose state differs
laws.falsifier: exhibit H,H' and pre-existing object o with o in ChangedExisting(H,H') and o notin M

laws.name: Pre-state dereference
laws.equation: eval_H'(old(a[i])) = eval_H(a[i]), whereas eval_H'(old(a)[i]) = eval_H'(a[i]); old affects the heap dereference, not parameter a
laws.falsifier: exhibit an increment call with post(a[i]) != pre(a[i]) + 1 after specifying the relation with old(a)[i]

laws.name: Fresh-result guarantee
laws.equation: fresh_H,H'(S) <=> forall o in S: o notin Alloc(H) and o in Alloc(H'), where S is a returned reference or set of references
laws.falsifier: exhibit returned o with o in Alloc(H) despite fresh(o)

laws.name: Read-frame stability
laws.equation: Agree(H,H',R) => f_H(args) = f_H'(args), where R is f's reads set and Agree means all fields or elements of objects in R are equal
laws.falsifier: exhibit H,H' agreeing on R with f_H(args) != f_H'(args)

entries.breaker_note: Use the frame and two-state laws from 14.0.0–14.0.4 to distinguish a correct result from one obtained by corrupting caller state. Test aliases explicitly, because frames name objects rather than the expressions used to reach them.
entries.implementer_note: Put every existing object that may change in modifies and every mutable dependency in reads. Place old around the actual field or array dereference, and promise fresh results when callers must be able to mutate newly allocated storage.

entries.title: Basic Array Modification
error_states: initialization exits with an untouched element or matrix cell — the initialized prefix or rows never cover the full index domain
inner matrix loop initializes the current row but clobbers an earlier row because its invariant omits the already completed rows
increment loop establishes the updated prefix but silently changes an unprocessed suffix element — post(a[i]) is not pre(a[i]) + 1
copy accepts src == dst but relates dst to the current source rather than the entry source — arbitrary in-place changes satisfy the apparent equality
left rotation is performed sequentially rather than simultaneously — later assignments read already overwritten elements

laws.name: Total initialization
laws.equation: InitArray(A,d) => forall i with 0 <= i < len(A): post(A[i]) = d; InitMatrix(M,d) => forall i,j in bounds: post(M[i,j]) = d
laws.falsifier: exhibit an output array or matrix with an in-bounds position k whose value is not d

laws.name: Processed-prefix and untouched-suffix invariant
laws.equation: I(n,A,A0) := 0 <= n <= N and (forall i with 0 <= i < n: A[i] = A0[i] + 1) and (forall i with n <= i < N: A[i] = A0[i]), where N=len(A) and A0 is the entry snapshot
laws.falsifier: exhibit a loop-head state satisfying the processed-prefix clause but with some i >= n having A[i] != A0[i]

laws.name: Alias-safe copy
laws.equation: len(src)=len(dst) => forall i with 0 <= i < len(src): post(dst[i]) = pre(src[i]), including the case src == dst
laws.falsifier: exhibit src,dst and i with post(dst[i]) != pre(src[i])

laws.name: Simultaneous aggregate update
laws.equation: forall-update A[i] := F(i,A) means post(A[i]) = F(i,pre(A)) for every selected i; for N>0, left rotation therefore satisfies post(A[i]) = pre(A[(i+1) mod N])
laws.falsifier: exhibit A and i with post(A[i]) computed from an already updated element rather than pre(A[(i+1) mod N])

entries.breaker_note: Attack both halves of each quantified update: the processed region and the region that must remain unchanged. Sections 14.1.2–14.1.4 make aliasing and snapshot semantics especially important test dimensions.
entries.implementer_note: Derive loop invariants by replacing a postcondition bound with the loop index, then preserve all earlier work in nested loops. When uniform updates are independent, use constructor or aggregate semantics so every right-hand side observes the same pre-update state.

entries.title: Summary
error_states: method returns the expected value after changing an array outside its declared write frame
function value changes after a mutation to an object outside its declared read frame
postcondition compares only post-state values and therefore fails to describe the intended relation to the input state
array loop proves a property of its processed prefix but exits before that prefix covers the whole array

laws.name: Frame separation
laws.equation: existing writes are confined to modifies M, and a function result depends only on reads R: ChangedExisting(H,H') subseteq M and Agree(H,H',R) => f_H(x)=f_H'(x)
laws.falsifier: exhibit either an existing changed object outside M or two heaps agreeing on R with different function results

laws.name: Two-state update contract
laws.equation: for an element transformer T, forall in-bounds i: post(A[i]) = T(pre(A[i]))
laws.falsifier: exhibit A and i with post(A[i]) != T(pre(A[i]))

laws.name: Fresh allocation boundary
laws.equation: fresh(S) => S intersect Alloc(pre) = {}, where S is a returned reference set
laws.falsifier: exhibit o in S intersect Alloc(pre)

laws.name: Loop coverage
laws.equation: I(n) := 0 <= n <= N and forall i with 0 <= i < n: P(i); I(n) and n=N => forall i with 0 <= i < N: P(i)
laws.falsifier: exhibit an exit state with I(n) and n != N, or an in-bounds i for which P(i) is false

entries.breaker_note: The chapter summary makes frames, old values, freshness, and quantified coverage part of the same mutation contract. A passing output-only test is insufficient if heap confinement or preservation is untested.
entries.implementer_note: Carry an entry snapshot into update properties, expose allocation freshness when needed by callers, and make loop exit turn the growing processed region into the full postcondition.

entries.title: Dutch National Flag
error_states: method returns colors in red-white-blue order but loses or duplicates an input color — sorted(post) holds while bag(post) != bag(pre)
red branch copies a[w] into the red region without preserving the displaced white element
blue branch overwrites a[b-1] instead of swapping — the blue value is duplicated and the displaced value is lost
segment markers overlap or leave a classified element in the wrong region
a branch neither increments w nor decrements b — the unsorted segment never shrinks

laws.name: Color ordering
laws.equation: SortedColor(A) := forall i,j with 0 <= i < j < N: Below(A[i],A[j]), where Below(c,d) := c=Red or c=d or d=Blue; DutchFlag requires SortedColor(post(A))
laws.falsifier: exhibit post(A) and i<j with not Below(A[i],A[j])

laws.name: Permutation conservation
laws.equation: bag(post(A)) = bag(pre(A)), where bag records each color's multiplicity
laws.falsifier: exhibit A with bag(post(A)) != bag(pre(A))

laws.name: Four-segment invariant
laws.equation: 0 <= r <= w <= b <= N and (forall i<r: A[i]=Red) and (forall r<=i<w: A[i]=White) and (forall b<=i<N: A[i]=Blue) and bag(A)=bag(A0)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a loop-head state violating a marker bound, a region color, or bag(A)=bag(A0)

laws.name: Unsorted-segment descent
laws.equation: V := b-w; while w<b, every branch establishes V' = V-1 and V >= 1
laws.falsifier: exhibit a guarded iteration with b'-w' >= b-w

entries.breaker_note: Require both order and multiset preservation; either property alone admits a broken sorter. Use the four-segment invariant and the exact b-w descent equation to generate branch-specific red tests.
entries.implementer_note: Treat r, w, and b as boundaries of half-open regions. Extend one classified region per iteration, swap rather than overwrite displaced values, and preserve the multiset as an always invariant.

entries.title: Selection Sort
error_states: method returns a sorted array that lost or duplicated elements — sorted(post) holds but bag(post) != bag(pre)
outer loop maintains a sorted prefix but chooses a new element smaller than that prefix because the split-point invariant is missing
inner loop's mindex falls outside the examined suffix or does not identify a minimum of the examined elements
inner or outer index fails to advance, so sorting does not terminate

laws.name: Selection-sort contract
laws.equation: Sorted(post(A)) and bag(post(A))=bag(pre(A)), where Sorted(A) := forall i,j with 0 <= i < j < N: A[i] <= A[j]
laws.falsifier: exhibit A with not Sorted(post(A)) or bag(post(A)) != bag(pre(A))

laws.name: Split-point invariant
laws.equation: SplitPoint(A,n) := forall i,j with 0 <= i < n <= j < N: A[i] <= A[j]
laws.falsifier: exhibit A,n,i,j with i<n<=j and A[i] > A[j]

laws.name: Minimum witness invariant
laws.equation: n <= mindex < m <= N and forall i with n <= i < m: A[mindex] <= A[i]
laws.falsifier: exhibit an inner-loop state with mindex outside [n,m) or some examined i with A[mindex] > A[i]

laws.name: Nested-loop descent
laws.equation: Vouter:=N-n decreases by 1 after each outer body, and Vinner:=N-m decreases by 1 after each inner body
laws.falsifier: exhibit a guarded outer or inner iteration with its corresponding variant not smaller afterward

entries.breaker_note: A sorted-prefix assertion is too weak: Section 15.1's decisive law is that every prefix element is also below every suffix element. Pair that split point with a witnessed minimum and multiset preservation.
entries.implementer_note: Keep mindex inside the examined interval and record its minimum property. Before extending the sorted prefix, preserve both its internal ordering and its ordering relative to the unsorted suffix.

entries.title: Quicksort
error_states: QuicksortAux returns with an inversion inside a[lo..hi)
partition or recursive sorting changes an element outside a[lo..hi)
partition swaps within the segment but loses or duplicates an element — the whole-array multiset changes
Partition returns p outside [lo,hi) or leaves a left element at least as large as the pivot or a right element smaller than it
recursive calls fail to shrink or destroy a split-point boundary, so recursion diverges or separately sorted segments do not compose

laws.name: Subrange sorting
laws.equation: forall i,j with lo <= i < j < hi: post(A[i]) <= post(A[j])
laws.falsifier: exhibit lo,hi,i,j with lo<=i<j<hi and post(A[i]) > post(A[j])

laws.name: Swap frame
laws.equation: SwapFrame(A,lo,hi) := (forall i with i<lo or hi<=i<N: post(A[i])=pre(A[i])) and bag(post(A))=bag(pre(A))
laws.falsifier: exhibit a call with an outside index changed or bag(post(A)) != bag(pre(A))

laws.name: Partition contract
laws.equation: lo <= p < hi and (forall i with lo <= i < p: A[i] < A[p]) and (forall i with p <= i < hi: A[p] <= A[i])
laws.falsifier: exhibit p outside [lo,hi), a left i with A[i]>=A[p], or a right i with A[i]<A[p]

laws.name: Split-point preservation
laws.equation: SplitPoint(pre(A),lo) and SplitPoint(pre(A),hi) => SplitPoint(post(A),lo) and SplitPoint(post(A),hi)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a call beginning with both split points and ending with either split point false

laws.name: Recursive-segment descent
