laws.equation: if hi-lo>=2 and lo<=p<hi, then p-lo < hi-lo and hi-(p+1) < hi-lo
laws.falsifier: exhibit lo,hi,p for which a recursive child has length greater than or equal to hi-lo

entries.breaker_note: Break Quicksort at its composition seams: Partition's pivot law, the two-state swap frame, preserved split points, and strict child-size decrease. These are the contracts that make the two recursive results compose into one sorted segment.
entries.implementer_note: Specify the exact subrange, preserve outside elements and the global multiset, and carry split points through every call. In Partition, maintain lower, unknown, and upper regions plus the swap frame, then return an in-range pivot that makes both recursive variants smaller.

entries.title: Summary
error_states: loop invariant is false initially, so the proof assumes a property the program never establishes
loop body preserves the invariant only on expected executions but fails for another state satisfying the invariant and guard
loop exits with its invariant true but the invariant is too weak to imply the postcondition
sorting routine establishes order but not preservation of input multiplicities

laws.name: Invariant initialization
laws.equation: Pre(s0) => I(s0), where s0 is the state at loop entry and I is the proposed invariant
laws.falsifier: exhibit s0 with Pre(s0) and not I(s0)

laws.name: Invariant inductiveness
laws.equation: forall states s: I(s) and Guard(s) => I(Step(s))
laws.falsifier: exhibit s with I(s) and Guard(s) and not I(Step(s))

laws.name: Exit adequacy
laws.equation: forall states s: I(s) and not Guard(s) => Post(s)
laws.falsifier: exhibit s with I(s) and not Guard(s) and not Post(s)

laws.name: In-situ sorting conjunction
laws.equation: Sorted(post(A)) and bag(post(A))=bag(pre(A))
laws.falsifier: exhibit A with an inversion in post(A) or unequal pre/post multiplicities

entries.breaker_note: Treat the invariant as a public algebraic claim over every state satisfying it, not merely states observed in one execution. Sorting tests must independently challenge order and element preservation.
entries.implementer_note: Record all loop-design decisions in the invariant, prove initialization and one arbitrary iteration, and ensure invariant plus guard negation yields the full postcondition.

entries.title: Checksums
error_states: constructor returns a machine whose data is nonempty or whose stored checksum disagrees with Hash(data)
Append extends the abstract data but fails to update cs, leaving Valid false and Checksum stale
Append updates cs correctly but fails to append exactly d to the ghost data model
Checksum returns a value other than Hash(data) despite the object being valid
method changes a different pre-existing object's fields although its frame names only this

laws.name: Checksum refinement invariant
laws.equation: Valid(m) <=> m.cs = Hash(m.data), where Hash(s)=SumChars(s) mod 137
laws.falsifier: exhibit m with Valid(m) claimed and m.cs != Hash(m.data)

laws.name: Incremental hash law
laws.equation: Hash(s+[ch]) = (Hash(s)+ord(ch)) mod 137, where [ch] is the one-character sequence and ord converts ch to int
laws.falsifier: exhibit s,ch with Hash(s+[ch]) != (Hash(s)+ord(ch)) mod 137

laws.name: Constructor establishment
laws.equation: post(Valid(m)) and post(m.data)="" and post(m.cs)=0
laws.falsifier: exhibit a newly constructed m with nonempty data, cs!=0, or not Valid(m)

laws.name: Append abstraction contract
laws.equation: Valid_pre(m) => Valid_post(m) and post(m.data)=pre(m.data)+d
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid m,d with invalid post-state or post(data) != pre(data)+d

laws.name: Checksum observation
laws.equation: Valid(m) => m.Checksum() = Hash(m.data)
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid m with m.Checksum() != Hash(m.data)

entries.breaker_note: Use the ghost data sequence as the client-visible model and cs as a private refinement checked by Valid (16.0.2). Append must preserve both the model extension and the refinement, regardless of how the module hides cs (16.0.4).
entries.implementer_note: Establish Valid in the constructor and require and restore it around every mutating method. For Append, maintain Valid together with data=old(data)+d[..i], using the one-character hash recurrence at each iteration.

entries.title: Tokenizer
error_states: Tokenizer advances n beyond the end of source, violating its object invariant
Read returns Whitespace instead of discarding the whitespace prefix
Read returns End when p is not the end of source, or reaches end of source without returning End
returned token differs from source[p..n] or contains a character outside its reported category
Read stops while the next character still belongs to the same category, returning a non-maximal token

laws.name: Category partition
laws.equation: for every character ch, exactly one cat in {Identifier,Number,Operator,Whitespace,Error} satisfies Is(ch,cat)
laws.falsifier: exhibit ch accepted by zero categories or by two distinct categories

laws.name: Category-recursion descent
laws.equation: rank(Error)=1 and rank(cat)=0 for cat!=Error; every recursive call made by Is(ch,Error) targets a cat with smaller rank
laws.falsifier: exhibit a recursive Is edge cat->cat2 with rank(cat2) >= rank(cat)

laws.name: Tokenizer validity
laws.equation: Valid(t) <=> 0 <= t.n <= len(t.source)
laws.falsifier: exhibit t with Valid(t) and t.n outside [0,len(source)]

laws.name: Whitespace and terminal boundaries
laws.equation: n0 <= p <= n1 <= N and (forall i with n0<=i<p: Is(source[i],Whitespace)) and cat!=Whitespace and (cat=End <=> p=N) and ((cat=End or cat=Error) <=> p=n1)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a Read result violating a bound, containing non-whitespace before p, returning Whitespace, or disagreeing with either terminal equivalence

laws.name: Exact maximal token
laws.equation: token=source[p:n1] and, if p<n1, then (forall i with p<=i<n1: Is(source[i],cat)) and (n1=N or not Is(source[n1],cat))
laws.falsifier: exhibit a nonempty returned token unequal to source[p:n1], containing a wrongly categorized character, or ending before another character of cat

entries.breaker_note: Treat the long Read postcondition in 16.1.2 as a packet of independently falsifiable boundary laws. Include empty input, whitespace-only input, Error, End, and a token followed by another character of the same category.
entries.implementer_note: Keep 0<=n<=|source| as the object invariant. Use one loop to establish the skipped-whitespace interval, choose the category at p, and use a second always-style loop to establish the token interval and maximal stopping condition.

entries.title: Simple Aggregate Objects
error_states: CoffeeMaker.Valid reads grinder or tank state not covered by its read frame — Valid changes after a supposedly irrelevant heap update
Restock or Dispense writes a constituent object absent from Repr, escaping the aggregate's advertised frame
constructor places an old aliased object in Repr while promising fresh(Repr), letting a new aggregate claim authority over caller-owned state
method adds a pre-existing undeclared object to Repr while promising that all new representation members are fresh
ChangeGrinder allocates a replacement but omits it from Repr, so the valid aggregate later mutates an object outside its frame

laws.name: Simple representation closure
laws.equation: Valid(cm) => cm in cm.Repr and cm.g in cm.Repr and Valid(cm.g) and cm.w in cm.Repr and Valid(cm.w)
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid cm missing itself or a constituent from Repr, or containing an invalid constituent

laws.name: Aggregate read stability
laws.equation: Agree(H,H',{cm} union cm.Repr) => Valid_H(cm)=Valid_H'(cm); when Valid(cm), Agree(H,H',cm.Repr) => Ready_H(cm)=Ready_H'(cm)
laws.falsifier: exhibit heaps agreeing on the stated frame with different Valid or Ready results

laws.name: Fresh construction
laws.equation: constructor(cm) => Valid(cm) and fresh(cm.Repr)
laws.falsifier: exhibit constructed cm with not Valid(cm) or some o in cm.Repr already allocated before construction

laws.name: Standard mutator protocol
laws.equation: Valid_pre(cm) => Valid_post(cm) and ChangedExisting(H,H') subseteq pre(cm.Repr) and fresh(post(cm.Repr)-pre(cm.Repr))
laws.falsifier: exhibit a mutator that invalidates cm, changes an existing object outside pre(Repr), or adds a nonfresh object to Repr

laws.name: Declared capture exception
laws.equation: InstallCustomGrinder(cm,g) => fresh(post(cm.Repr)-pre(cm.Repr)-{g})
laws.falsifier: exhibit an old object o added to Repr with o!=g and o notin pre(Repr)

entries.breaker_note: Make Repr observable only as the aggregate's abstract authority set, then test closure, frame confinement, and freshness. Sections 16.2.2 and 16.2.5 distinguish standard fresh growth from the explicit capture of a client-supplied constituent.
entries.implementer_note: Define Valid with reads this,Repr and order membership checks before constituent Valid calls. Constructors establish fresh(Repr); mutators preserve Valid and promise that newly added representation objects are fresh, with explicit exclusions for captured parameters.

entries.title: Full Aggregate Objects
error_states: grinder and water-tank representation sets overlap — AddBeans modifies shared state and invalidates the water tank
CoffeeMaker itself belongs to a child's Repr — a child method can change the owner's fields and smash the owner's invariant
child Repr expands after a call but CoffeeMaker.Repr is not expanded, breaking the required subset relation and future frame confinement
constructor's final Repr omits part of a child's representation set, so the parent does not own its full implementation graph
validity predicate hides that every valid object belongs to its own Repr, preventing parent closure from accounting for the constituent object itself

laws.name: Exposed self-membership
laws.equation: Valid(o) => o in o.Repr for every aggregate object o
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid o with o notin o.Repr

laws.name: Nested representation closure
laws.equation: Valid(cm) => cm in R and g in R and Rg subseteq R and cm notin Rg and Valid(g) and w in R and Rw subseteq R and cm notin Rw and Valid(w), where R=cm.Repr, Rg=g.Repr, and Rw=w.Repr
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid cm violating any containment, owner-exclusion, or constituent-validity conjunct

laws.name: Sibling separation
laws.equation: Valid(cm) => g.Repr intersect w.Repr = {}
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid cm and object o with o in g.Repr and o in w.Repr

laws.name: Disjoint-frame noninterference
laws.equation: ChangedExisting(H,H') subseteq g.Repr and g.Repr intersect w.Repr={} => Valid_H(w)=Valid_H'(w)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a g-framed update over disjoint representations that changes the truth of w.Valid()

laws.name: Parent-frame refresh
laws.equation: after constituent calls, post(cm.Repr)=pre(cm.Repr) union post(g.Repr) union post(w.Repr), which implies post(g.Repr) subseteq post(cm.Repr) and post(w.Repr) subseteq post(cm.Repr)
laws.falsifier: exhibit a post-state with an object in a child's Repr but not in cm.Repr

entries.breaker_note: Attack nested aggregates through overlap, owner capture, and child-frame growth. The separation and subset laws in 16.3.3 are what justify sequential calls on independent constituents.
entries.implementer_note: Construct the full parent frame only after child frames are available, using locals in the first constructor phase or assigning after new; (16.3.2). After any child may expand its Repr, union the updated child sets back into the parent's Repr.

entries.title: Summary
error_states: Valid is true while this is absent from Repr, so the object's own fields are outside its advertised frame
two simple constituents alias or dynamic constituent frames overlap, allowing one operation to invalidate another constituent
constructor returns a representation set containing an object allocated before construction
mutating method preserves its result but changes an existing object outside pre(Repr) or adds an old object to Repr
function reads mutable state outside Repr, so its value changes while its declared frame is unchanged

laws.name: Canonical validity shape
laws.equation: Valid(o) => o in R; each simple constituent a satisfies a in R and Valid(a); each dynamic constituent b satisfies b in R and b.Repr subseteq R and o notin b.Repr and Valid(b); distinct constituent representations are pairwise disjoint, where R=o.Repr
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid o violating self-membership, constituent closure, owner exclusion, validity, or pairwise separation

laws.name: Constructor protocol
laws.equation: post(Valid(o)) and fresh(post(o.Repr))
laws.falsifier: exhibit a constructed o that is invalid or has a nonfresh representation member

laws.name: Function frame law
laws.equation: Valid(o) and Agree(H,H',o.Repr) => F_H(o,x)=F_H'(o,x)
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid o and heaps agreeing on Repr with different F results

laws.name: Mutating-method protocol
laws.equation: Valid_pre(o) => Valid_post(o) and ChangedExisting(H,H') subseteq pre(o.Repr) and fresh(post(o.Repr)-pre(o.Repr))
laws.falsifier: exhibit a valid call that returns invalid, changes an existing object outside pre(Repr), or adds a nonfresh representation member

entries.breaker_note: Use 16.4 as the canonical dynamic-frame checklist: closure and separation in Valid, fresh construction, Repr-bounded reads and writes, and fresh representation growth. A deviation needs an explicit alternative contract.
entries.implementer_note: Instantiate the idiom mechanically, then strengthen it only for the class's actual topology. Keep Valid as reads this,Repr, establish the complete frame after constructor phase one, and restore closure whenever a child frame grows.

entries.title: Lazily Initialized Arrays
data_structures: backing arrays a, b, and c
error_states: Update writes c[n] when n == N, causing an out-of-bounds failure on a full logical array.
Get treats an uninitialized b[i] value as initialized, returns a[i] instead of default, or misses a previously updated value.
Update changes Elements at the wrong index or changes a second index, so the concrete arrays and ghost sequence disagree.
Two LazyArray instances share backing storage, so updating one changes the other's Get result.

laws.name: Abstract read
laws.equation: For valid A and 0 <= i < N_A, Get_A(i) == Elements_A[i], where N_A == |Elements_A|.
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid A and i with Get_A(i) != Elements_A[i]

laws.name: Functional update
laws.equation: After Update_A(i,x), Elements_after == Elements_before[i := x], and for every j != i, Elements_after[j] == Elements_before[j].
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid A, i, j, and x with j != i and Elements_after[j] != Elements_before[j]

laws.name: Reverse-index cardinality
laws.falsifier: exhibit a valid A and i with Init_A(i) != (0 <= b_A[i] < n_A && c_A[b_A[i]] == i), or with n_A != |s_A|

laws.name: There is room
laws.equation: Valid(A) && 0 <= i < N_A && !Init_A(i) ==> n_A < N_A.
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid A and i with 0 <= i < N_A, !Init_A(i), and n_A == N_A

laws.name: Finite prefix cardinality
laws.equation: Upto(k) == {j | 0 <= j < k} and |Upto(k)| == k for every natural k.
laws.falsifier: exhibit k with Upto(k) != {j | 0 <= j < k} or |Upto(k)| != k

laws.name: Fresh representation isolation
laws.equation: Repr_A !! Repr_B ==> Update_A(i,x) leaves Elements_B unchanged, where !! means set disjointness.
laws.falsifier: exhibit disjoint valid A and B where Update_A(i,x) changes Elements_B

entries.breaker_note: Use the contracts from 17.0.0, the reverse-index invariant from 17.0.3-17.0.4, and the room/cardinality proof from 17.0.6 as red-test targets.
entries.implementer_note: Maintain immutable N and Repr from 17.0.2 and the central Elements-to-storage invariant from 17.0.4. Discharge the full-array boundary with Upto, SetCardinalities, and ThereIsRoom from 17.0.6.

entries.title: Extensible Array
error_states: Append leaves front full at length == M + 256 instead of moving it into the depot, breaking the boundary invariant.
Get or Update uses the wrong depot array or wrong quotient/remainder index, returning or changing the wrong element.
Append increments length but does not append exactly one element to Elements, losing or duplicating values.
front or two depot arrays alias, so an update through one logical position corrupts another position.
Recursive Get or Append does not descend to a smaller representation or sequence measure, causing nontermination.

laws.name: Depot/front boundary
laws.equation: M == (if depot == null then 0 else 256 * |depot.Elements|) && M <= length && length < M + 256 && (length == M <=> front == null).
laws.falsifier: exhibit a valid-looking state with length == M + 256, or length == M and front != null

laws.name: Storage projection
laws.equation: For 0 <= i < M, Elements[i] == depot.Elements[i / 256][i % 256]; for M <= i < length, Elements[i] == front[i - M], where / is integer division.
laws.falsifier: exhibit i in range with Elements[i] != depot.Elements[i / 256][i % 256] or Elements[i] != front[i - M]

laws.name: Append preservation
laws.equation: After Append(t), Elements_after == Elements_before + [t] and length_after == length_before + 1.
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid A and t with Elements_after != Elements_before + [t]

laws.name: Functional update
laws.equation: After Update(i,t), Elements_after == Elements_before[i := t], with every other index unchanged.
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid A, i, j, and t with j != i and Elements_after[j] != Elements_before[j]

laws.name: Representation separation
laws.equation: Every depot array is in Repr but outside depot.Repr, is distinct from front, and is distinct from every other depot array.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a state with front == depot.Elements[j] or depot.Elements[j] == depot.Elements[k] for j != k

laws.name: Recursive descent measure
laws.equation: For recursive Get, depot.Repr < Repr; for recursive Append, |depot.Elements| < |this.Elements|, where < is strict subset or strict integer decrease.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a recursive call whose selected measure is not strictly smaller

entries.breaker_note: Use the contract from 17.1.0 and the partition, aliasing, and full-front invariants from 17.1.1-17.1.3 as the red-test oracle.
entries.implementer_note: Make the null/full boundary decisions explicit in the invariant from 17.1.1-17.1.2. Implement the depot projection first, flush exactly at 256 elements, and supply the sequence-size decrease for Append from 17.1.3.

entries.title: Binary Search Tree for a Map
error_states: Lookup returns None for a present key, Some for an absent key, or the wrong value for a present key.
Add replaces the requested key but drops unrelated map entries or stores the new key in a subtree that search cannot reach.
A left key is not less than the node key or a right key is not greater, so later binary search skips an existing entry.
Remove on a root with two children loses a subtree, chooses the wrong successor, or returns null for a nonempty result map.
Child representations alias or contain the parent, or recursive Add/Remove fails to descend and does not terminate.

laws.name: Node map abstraction
laws.equation: For valid node n, M_n == Union(Union(map[n.key := n.value], left_n), right_n), where Union(m,null) == m and Union(m,q) == m + M_q.
laws.falsifier: exhibit valid n with M_n missing a child entry, containing an extra entry, or assigning the wrong value

laws.name: Binary-search ordering
laws.equation: Every l in M_left.Keys satisfies l < n.key, and every r in M_right.Keys satisfies n.key < r.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a valid-looking node with l in M_left.Keys and l >= n.key, or r in M_right.Keys and n.key >= r

laws.name: Lookup correctness
laws.equation: key in M.Keys ==> Lookup(key) == Some(M[key]); key !in M.Keys ==> Lookup(key) == None.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a valid tree and key violating either branch

laws.name: Add map update
laws.equation: After Add(key,value), M_after == M_before[key := value].
laws.falsifier: exhibit a valid tree where an unrelated map entry changes or the requested entry is absent or wrong

laws.name: Remove map update
laws.equation: For newMap == old(M) - {key}, Remove(key) returns null iff |newMap.Keys| == 0, otherwise returns n != null with n.M == newMap.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a valid tree where the returned map differs from old(M) - {key} or null is returned for a nonempty result

laws.name: Minimum witness
laws.equation: Min() == (k,val) implies k in M.Keys, M[k] == val, and forall k' in M.Keys, k <= k'.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a valid nonempty tree whose Min() key is absent, has the wrong value, or exceeds another key

laws.name: Union cardinality
laws.equation: For u == Union(m,n), m.Keys <= u.Keys and therefore |m.Keys| <= |u.Keys|.
laws.falsifier: exhibit m,n with a key in m.Keys absent from u.Keys or with |m.Keys| > |u.Keys|

laws.name: Representation descent
laws.equation: For each non-null child c of node n, c.Repr < n.Repr; left.Repr !! right.Repr and n !in c.Repr, where < is strict subset.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a child with the same representation set as its parent, overlapping sibling representation, or the parent in the child representation

entries.breaker_note: Use 17.2.0, 17.2.2, and 17.2.4 to test map preservation, ordering, deletion surgery, representation separation, and recursive descent.
entries.implementer_note: Build the Node.Valid invariant before the recursive methods. Use Repr as the explicit decreases metric, and prove Remove's empty-result obligation through Union's key-subset and cardinality lemmas.

entries.title: Iterator for the Map
error_states: GetNext returns a key twice, returns a key not in the container, or silently omits a pending key.
GetNext returns None while RemainingKeys is nonempty, or returns Some when no key remains.
GetNext returns the right key with a value different from bst.M[key].
GetNext mutates an object in bst.Repr or an iterator remains usable after the container representation changes.
Push or GetNext loses a right subtree from the stack, violates SValid, or loops without consuming pending work.

laws.name: Exact key consumption
laws.equation: At construction R0 == bst.M.Keys; while bst is unchanged, R0 == ReturnedKeys + RemainingKeys and ReturnedKeys !! RemainingKeys.
laws.falsifier: exhibit an iterator state with a returned key still in RemainingKeys, or with a key in R0 in neither set

laws.name: Option exhaustion
laws.equation: GetNext() == None <=> old(RemainingKeys) == {}; GetNext() == Some((k,v)) => k in old(RemainingKeys).
laws.falsifier: exhibit a valid iterator with old(RemainingKeys) nonempty and result None, or with result Some(k,v) and k not pending

laws.name: Returned value soundness
laws.equation: GetNext() == Some((k,v)) ==> v == bst.M[k].
laws.falsifier: exhibit a valid iterator returning Some(k,v) with v != bst.M[k]

laws.name: Pending-set transition
laws.equation: For Some((k,v)), RemainingKeys_after == RemainingKeys_before - {k}; for None, RemainingKeys_after == RemainingKeys_before == {}.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a call that removes more than k, removes no k, or changes RemainingKeys on None

laws.name: Stack representation
laws.equation: SValid(Nil,R) <=> R == {}; for Cons(node,next), m == Union(map[node.key := node.value], node.right), m.Keys <= R, and SValid(next,R - m.Keys).
laws.falsifier: exhibit SValid(stack,R) with Nil and R nonempty, or with a Cons whose represented keys are not contained in R

laws.name: Iterator frame and invalidation
laws.equation: writes(GetNext) <= Repr - bst.Repr; bst.Repr_after != bst.Repr_before means prior iterator Valid need not hold.
laws.falsifier: exhibit GetNext changing bst.Repr, or a container mutation after which the old iterator still claims Valid without revalidation

laws.name: Push postcondition
laws.equation: After Push(nn), RemainingKeys_after == RemainingKeys_before + (if nn == null then {} else nn.M.Keys), with disjoint operands.
laws.falsifier: exhibit Push that omits a key from nn.M.Keys, adds a duplicate, or changes an old pending key

laws.name: Loop progress
laws.equation: Each non-null Push iteration sets S_after == S_before - m.Keys with m.Keys != {}, hence S_after < S_before.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a loop iteration with m.Keys == {} or S_after not a strict subset of S_before

entries.breaker_note: Turn the contracts in 17.3.0 and the stack/progress invariants in 17.3.3-17.3.6 into exactness, invalidation, and no-duplicate tests.
entries.implementer_note: Represent remaining work with immutable List in 17.3.2, preserve SValid while pushing and popping, and use the decreasing ghost set S from 17.3.4 to discharge the loop.

entries.title: Summary
error_states: A client method returns the promised abstract result but leaves Valid() false, so later clients rely on a broken representation.
A callee writes outside the caller's declared representation frame, corrupting an unrelated aggregate.
A container mutation leaves an outstanding iterator apparently valid even though its cached traversal state is stale.

laws.name: Validity preservation
laws.equation: Valid_before && Pre_call ==> Valid_after for every client-facing method.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a valid receiver and permitted call with Valid_after == false

laws.name: Representation frame
laws.equation: writes(call) <= Repr(receiver), or writes(GetNext) <= Repr(iterator) - Repr(container).
laws.falsifier: exhibit a permitted call that changes an object outside its declared frame

laws.name: Dependent iterator invalidation
laws.equation: Repr(container)_after != Repr(container)_before ==> prior Iterator.Valid need not hold.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a changed container representation with an old iterator still accepted as valid

entries.breaker_note: Use the summary's common Valid and Repr rules as cross-case oracles for postcondition preservation and heap isolation.
entries.implementer_note: Treat Valid as the client boundary and Repr as the aggregate ownership boundary. Preserve dependent-object assumptions explicitly when dynamic frames overlap.

entries.title: Expressions
error_states: Map merge gives priority to the left operand, so updating an existing key leaves the old value.
A sequence update changes an index other than the target or uses the wrong slice endpoint.
An array or sequence slice includes one extra element or omits the upper boundary, breaking a range-based search.
Set, multiset, or sequence union/difference uses the wrong membership, multiplicity, or concatenation semantics.

laws.name: Set union and difference
laws.equation: x in (A + B) <=> (x in A || x in B), and x in (A - B) <=> (x in A && x !in B), for sets A,B.
laws.falsifier: exhibit A,B,x violating either membership equivalence

laws.name: Right-priority map merge
laws.equation: For u == m + n, u.Keys == m.Keys + n.Keys and u[k] == n[k] if k in n.Keys, otherwise u[k] == m[k].
laws.falsifier: exhibit maps m,n with k in n.Keys and (m + n)[k] != n[k]

laws.name: Sequence update and slice length
laws.falsifier: exhibit E,i,j,v,lo,hi violating target preservation, non-target preservation, or slice length

laws.name: Array-to-sequence projection
laws.equation: For array E, E[..] == E[0..E.Length] and |E[..]| == E.Length.
laws.falsifier: exhibit an array E where E[..] omits, duplicates, or reorders an element

entries.breaker_note: Retain the operator semantics needed by the Chapter 17 contracts; A.0-A.1 declaration and statement syntax is not part of the catalog.
entries.implementer_note: Use these collection equations as the shared meaning of map updates, sequence abstraction fields, and array range projections.

entries.title: Boolean Values and Negation
error_states: Negation maps true to true or false to false, so a guard's branch condition is inverted incorrectly.
Double negation changes a predicate, causing a proof or assertion to accept the opposite state.
The implementation treats false and !true as different boolean values.

laws.name: Negation of true
laws.equation: !true == false.
laws.falsifier: exhibit evaluation of !true != false

laws.name: Double negation
laws.equation: !!X == X for every boolean expression X.
laws.falsifier: exhibit boolean X with !!X != X

laws.name: False as negated true
laws.equation: true == !false.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a boolean evaluation where !false != true

entries.breaker_note: Use the three negation identities as primitive assertion oracles before testing larger Boolean formulas.
entries.implementer_note: Normalize nested negation and replace !true or !false immediately when discharging Boolean proof obligations.

entries.title: Conjunction
error_states: A conjunction passes when only one required condition is true, behaving like disjunction.
A compound conjunction changes value when operands are reordered or regrouped.
A contradiction X && !X evaluates true, allowing an impossible branch to execute.
A negated conjunction is distributed incorrectly, accepting a state where only part of the required formula holds.

laws.name: Unit and zero
laws.equation: true && X == X, and false && X == false.
laws.falsifier: exhibit boolean X violating either identity

laws.name: Semilattice laws
laws.falsifier: exhibit booleans X,Y,Z violating idempotence, commutativity, or associativity

laws.name: Distribution
laws.falsifier: exhibit booleans X,Y,Z with unequal sides

laws.name: Law of contradiction
laws.equation: X && !X == false.
laws.falsifier: exhibit boolean X with X && !X != false

entries.breaker_note: Use unit, zero, semilattice, distribution, and contradiction laws to catch incorrect Boolean guards and invariant conjunctions.
entries.implementer_note: Simplify conjunctions with units and zeros, regroup freely only for Boolean value proofs, and use contradiction to close impossible branches.

entries.title: Predicates and Well-Definedness
error_states: A guard evaluates a division, array index, or dereference on the right even though a left short-circuit condition should have prevented it.
A logically equivalent reordering of a conjunction is accepted even though the reordered expression can divide by zero or dereference null.
A verifier proves the Boolean value of a formula without proving that every evaluated operand is defined.

laws.name: Short-circuit well-definedness
laws.equation: WD(X && Y) == WD(X) && (!Val(X) || WD(Y)); WD(X || Y) == WD(X) && (Val(X) || WD(Y)); WD(X ==> Y) == WD(X) && (!Val(X) || WD(Y)), where WD means well-defined and Val is the Boolean value when defined.
laws.falsifier: exhibit d == 0, X == (100 <= d), and Y == (a == c / d): WD(X && Y) holds but WD(Y && X) fails

laws.name: Value commutativity under definition
laws.equation: If WD(X && Y) && WD(Y && X), then Val(X && Y) == Val(Y && X), but well-definedness may differ.
laws.falsifier: exhibit expressions X,Y whose Boolean values commute but one operand order is undefined

laws.name: Guard-before-dependent-expression
laws.equation: X && Y is safe only when WD(X) and (!Val(X) || WD(Y)); the left operand must establish Y's definedness when X is true.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a false guard followed by an evaluated division-by-zero, null dereference, or out-of-range index

entries.breaker_note: Make definedness part of the red test: Boolean equivalence alone does not justify reordering short-circuit predicates.
entries.implementer_note: Place range, non-null, and nonzero guards before dependent expressions, and discharge WD obligations in left-to-right order.

entries.title: Disjunction and Proof Format
error_states: A disjunction evaluates false when one operand is true, or true when both operands are false.
A De Morgan or distribution step changes a guard's truth value.
A proof calculation reaches a final expression using a step that is not an equality, so the claimed theorem is unsound.
A disjunction is grouped incorrectly and changes the result of a nested guard.

laws.name: De Morgan
laws.falsifier: exhibit booleans X,Y with either De Morgan equality false

laws.name: Unit, zero, and semilattice laws
laws.equation: false || X == X; true || X == true; X || X == X; X || Y == Y || X; X || (Y || Z) == (X || Y) || Z.
laws.falsifier: exhibit booleans X,Y,Z violating one identity

laws.name: Disjunction distribution
laws.falsifier: exhibit booleans X,Y,Z with unequal sides

laws.name: Excluded middle
laws.equation: X || !X == true.
laws.falsifier: exhibit boolean X with X || !X != true

laws.name: Proof-calculation transitivity
laws.equation: E0 == E1 && E1 == E2 ==> E0 == E2; an annotated equality chain preserves the endpoint value.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a calculation containing a step E_i != E_(i+1) while claiming E0 == En

entries.breaker_note: Use the Boolean identities as algebraic red tests and require every proof-calculation step to preserve equality.
entries.implementer_note: Rewrite disjunctions with De Morgan or distribution when useful, then annotate each equality step with the law that justifies it.

entries.title: Implication
error_states: An implication is implemented as conjunction, so a false antecedent incorrectly makes the formula false.
A contract accepts a postcondition without its precondition, or uses the contrapositive in the wrong direction.
Shunting a premise across implication changes a required guard and admits an invalid state.
Right-associative implication is parsed as left-associative, changing a chained proof obligation.

laws.name: Implication definition
laws.falsifier: exhibit booleans X,Y with (X ==> Y) != (!X || Y)

laws.name: Modus ponens
laws.falsifier: exhibit booleans X,Y violating the equality

laws.name: Contrapositive
laws.falsifier: exhibit booleans X,Y with unequal implications

laws.name: Shunting
laws.falsifier: exhibit booleans X,Y,Z with unequal sides

laws.name: Implication distribution
laws.falsifier: exhibit booleans X,Y,Z violating the distribution equality

entries.breaker_note: Turn implication definitions, contraposition, shunting, and distribution into tests for contract direction and guard movement.
entries.implementer_note: Read X ==> Y as 'assuming X, establish Y'; use the definition or shunting only after checking the operator precedence and direction.

entries.title: Proving Implications
error_states: A proof claims X ==> X without establishing the Boolean tautology, so a reflexive obligation remains unsolved.
A transitive proof uses X ==> Y and Y ==> Z but concludes the reverse direction or skips one premise.
A proof treats an assumed antecedent as if it were already the consequent, accepting an invalid invariant or postcondition.
A proof calculation contains a non-equality step but reports the endpoint as established.

laws.name: Reflexivity
laws.equation: X ==> X == true.
laws.falsifier: exhibit boolean X with X ==> X != true

laws.name: Implication transitivity
laws.falsifier: exhibit boolean X,Y,Z where both premises hold but X ==> Z is false

laws.name: Antecedent discharge pattern
laws.equation: To establish A ==> B, assume A and derive B; equivalently, A && (A ==> B) == A && B.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a purported proof of A ==> B that has A true but B false

entries.breaker_note: Use reflexivity and transitivity as theorem-level tests, and reject proofs that do not explicitly establish the consequent under the antecedent.
entries.implementer_note: For a large implication, assume its antecedent and simplify from that context; for chains, prove each arrow and compose them.

entries.title: Free Variables and Substitution
error_states: Substitution replaces a bound occurrence, changing the scope of a quantifier.
A free variable in the replacement becomes captured by a quantifier in the target expression.
Simultaneous substitutions are applied sequentially, so one replacement changes the input of another.
Alpha-renaming a bound variable changes the formula's meaning instead of preserving it.

laws.name: Alpha-renaming
laws.equation: alpha(E,y,w) == E when w is fresh and only a bound variable y is renamed.
laws.falsifier: exhibit E and fresh w where alpha-renaming changes E's value

laws.name: Free-occurrence substitution
laws.equation: (x < 100 && 20 <= Fib(y))[y := 2*x + y] == x < 100 && 20 <= Fib(2*x + y), with only free y replaced.
laws.falsifier: exhibit an expression where substitution changes a bound occurrence of y

laws.name: Capture avoidance
laws.equation: (forall y :: P(x,y))[x := y] == forall w :: P(y,w), where w is fresh and w notin FV(y).
laws.falsifier: exhibit E == forall y :: P(x,y) where naive substitution yields forall y :: P(y,y) instead of alpha-renaming

laws.name: Simultaneous substitution
laws.falsifier: exhibit replacements whose sequential application gives a result different from simultaneous substitution

entries.breaker_note: Test substitution on bound and free occurrences separately; capture and sequential replacement are correctness failures, not cosmetic differences.
entries.implementer_note: Alpha-rename binders before substitution, replace only free occurrences, and apply multi-variable substitutions simultaneously.

entries.title: Universal Quantification
error_states: A universal assertion passes after checking one witness even though another value violates the predicate.
The one-point rule substitutes the wrong value or leaves the quantified variable in the result.
An unused variable is eliminated over an empty type, turning forall x :: true into an incorrect true claim.
A bounded array or search invariant includes the wrong endpoint or omits the first or last element.

laws.name: Universal distribution
laws.equation: forall x :: (E && F) == (forall x :: E) && (forall x :: F).
laws.falsifier: exhibit predicates E,F and a domain where the two sides differ

laws.name: Universal one-point rule
laws.equation: forall x :: (x == F ==> E) == E[x := F], provided x is not free in F.
laws.falsifier: exhibit E,F where the quantified formula differs from E[x := F]

laws.name: Unused and constant variables
laws.equation: forall x :: E == E when x is not free in E and x's type is nonempty; forall x :: true == true.
laws.falsifier: exhibit an empty type for the first rule or a non-true result for the constant rule

laws.name: Range decomposition
laws.equation: For m < n, forall i :: (m <= i < n ==> P(i)) == P(m) && (forall i :: (m + 1 <= i < n ==> P(i))).
laws.falsifier: exhibit m,n,P where the decomposition includes an extra index or omits an index

entries.breaker_note: Use universal laws to expose quantifier-range off-by-one errors and claims that validate only a witness instead of every element.
entries.implementer_note: Split bounded ranges at a concrete endpoint, apply the one-point rule when a range pins a variable, and preserve nonempty-type side conditions.

entries.title: Existential Quantification
error_states: An existential assertion is true with no witness or false even though a valid witness satisfies the predicate.
Negating a universal or existential condition produces the wrong quantifier or fails to negate the predicate.
Factoring an independent condition out of an existential loses the witness-dependent condition.
A bounded search existential includes the wrong endpoint or misses the only witness.

laws.name: Quantifier De Morgan
laws.equation: !(forall x :: P) == exists x :: !P; !(exists x :: P) == forall x :: !P.
laws.falsifier: exhibit a domain and predicate where either negation equality fails

laws.name: Existential one-point rule
laws.equation: exists x :: (x == F && E) == E[x := F], provided x is not free in F.
laws.falsifier: exhibit E,F where the existential result differs from E[x := F]

laws.name: Independent-condition extraction
laws.equation: exists x :: (E && F) == E && (exists x :: F), when x is not free in E and the type is nonempty.
laws.falsifier: exhibit E,F where factoring E changes the existential truth value

laws.name: Unused and false existential
laws.equation: exists x :: E == E when x is not free in E and the type is nonempty; exists x :: false == false.
laws.falsifier: exhibit an empty type for the unused-variable rule or a result other than false for exists x :: false

laws.name: Existential range decomposition
laws.equation: For m < n, exists i :: (m <= i < n && P(i)) == P(m) || (exists i :: (m + 1 <= i < n && P(i))).
laws.falsifier: exhibit m,n,P where the decomposition loses or invents a witness

entries.breaker_note: Use witness soundness, quantifier duality, and range decomposition to catch false positives, false negatives, and search-boundary defects.
entries.implementer_note: Provide an explicit witness for existential goals, use De Morgan to switch quantifiers safely, and split bounded searches without changing their endpoints.
